source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $N\ge1$, and for $0\le n\le N$ let $U_n\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_n}$ be open. A finite parameterized state-step graph consists of a $C^1$ initial map $x_0:\Theta\to U_0$ and $C^1$ step maps $\Psi_n:U_n\times\Theta\to U_{n+1}$ for $0\le n<N$, such that the recursion $x_{n+1}(\theta)=\Psi_n(x_n(\theta),\theta)$ is defined for every $\theta$ in the chosen parameter neighborhood. A $C^1$ running objective consists of maps $\ell_n:U_n\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ and a terminal objective $\phi:U_N\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$, all $C^1$. Its reduced objective is
$$J(\theta)=\phi(x_N(\theta),\theta)+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\ell_n(x_n(\theta),\theta).$$
The maps and objective define one finite real-arithmetic graph. A gradient of this graph is the derivative of this finite composition; it is not the derivative of an exact implicit solution unless the step map itself is that solution map.
source_evidence.case_anchor: A finite C1 state graph defines its reduced objective and exact graph derivative; it does not characterize the derivative of a stopped solver or an exact implicit solution.

source_evidence.fullclaim: Let $V$ be a real Hilbert space, let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and write $V^*$ for the continuous real dual. A parameter-dependent coercive elliptic variational problem is a family of bounded bilinear forms $a_\theta:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ and bounded linear functionals $\ell_\theta\in V^*$ such that, on each parameter neighborhood under discussion, $\|a_\theta\|\le M$ and $a_\theta(v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2$ for fixed $M<\infty$ and $\alpha>0$. Operator-norm $C^1$ data means that the maps $\theta\mapsto A_\theta\in\mathcal L(V,V^*)$, $A_\theta u:=a_\theta(u,\cdot)$, and $\theta\mapsto\ell_\theta\in V^*$ are continuously Fréchet differentiable. A state at $\theta$ is a vector $u_\theta\in V$ satisfying $a_\theta(u_\theta,v)=\ell_\theta(v)$ for every $v\in V$. When a state is specified, a $C^1$ objective $J:V\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ defines the reduced objective $j(\theta)=J(u_\theta,\theta)$. This definition alone asserts neither state existence nor uniqueness of an optimizer.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $(V,H,V^*)$ be the real evolution triple and let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open. A parameter-dependent parabolic variational problem specifies, for each $\theta\in\Theta$, a bilinear form $a_\theta(t;\cdot,\cdot)$ and data $f_\theta\in L^2(0,T;V^*)$, $u_{0,\theta}\in H$. A state is a function $u_\theta\in W(0,T;V)$ with continuous $H$ trace, $u_\theta(0)=u_{0,\theta}$, and
$$\langle u_\theta'(t),v\rangle_{V^*,V}+a_\theta(t;u_\theta(t),v)=\langle f_\theta(t),v\rangle_{V^*,V}$$
for every $v\in V$ and almost every $t$. When a state is specified, a differentiable terminal and running objective $\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)+\int_0^T L(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)\,dt$ defines its reduced objective. This definition does not assert existence, parameter differentiability, or optimality.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ and $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d\times\Theta$ be open, and let $f:D\to\mathbb R^d$ be continuously differentiable. Let $V_\theta\subseteq\Theta$ be open and $u_0:V_\theta\to\mathbb R^d$ be $C^1$. Assume there is a bounded convex open set $O\subset D$ with compact closure in $D$ such that for every $\theta\in V_\theta$ the unique solution of $u'=f(t,u,\theta)$, $u(0)=u_0(\theta)$, exists on $[0,T]$, and all triples $(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)$ lie in $O$. Then $\theta\mapsto u_\theta$ is $C^1$ as a map to $C([0,T];\mathbb R^d)$. For any $\theta_0\in V_\theta$, its tangent matrix $S(t)=D_\theta u_\theta(t)|_{\theta=\theta_0}$ is the unique solution of
$$S'(t)=D_u f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0)S(t)+D_\theta f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0),\qquad S(0)=D u_0(\theta_0).$$
The result is local to the stated common compact tube and claims no differentiability outside it.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $J$ and $J_h$ be the continuous and finite state-step objectives of [[thm-continuous-ode-adjoint-gradient-formula]] and [[thm-discrete-adjoint-gradient-recursion]], respectively, and put $h=T/N$. Let $q(t,u,p)=D_\theta\ell(t,u,\theta)^T+D_\theta f(t,u,\theta)^Tp$ be the continuous running-gradient vector, evaluated on its exact state and adjoint as $q(t):=q(t,u(t),p(t))$. Suppose the exact and numerical state/adjoint pairs lie in a common tube and
$$\max_n\bigl(\|u_n-u(t_n)\|_2+\|p_n-p(t_n)\|_2\bigr)\le C_xh^p.$$
For the state part of this bound, it is sufficient that the hypotheses of [[thm-global-error-from-one-step-defect-and-stability]] hold with a uniform $O(h^{p+1})$ exact-start defect; the coefficient conditions of [[prop-explicit-rk-order-conditions-through-four]] supply that defect for an explicit Runge--Kutta method of order $p\le4$ under that item's $C^4$ and common-tube assumptions. No cited state-error result supplies the adjoint part, which is an independent hypothesis here. Write $b$ and $b_h$ for the column initial/terminal contribution vectors in the continuous and discrete gradient formulas. Assume the discrete running-gradient terms admit vectors $\widehat q_n$ and nonnegative weights $w_n$, $0\le n\le N$, with
$$\nabla J_h=b_h+\sum_{n=0}^N w_n\widehat q_n,\qquad \nabla J=b+\int_0^Tq(t)\,dt,\qquad \sum_{n=0}^Nw_n=T.$$
The weighted discrete representation is an explicit premise; it is not implied by the generic finite state-step adjoint recursion. Suppose
$$\|\widehat q_n-q(t_n,u_n,p_n)\|_2\le C_dh^p,\qquad \|b_h-b\|_2\le C_bh^p,$$
and that the same weights give the quadrature $Q_h(q)=\sum_{n=0}^Nw_nq(t_n)$ satisfying
$$\left\|Q_h(q)-\int_0^Tq(t)\,dt\right\|_2\le C_Qh^p.$$
If $q$ is Lipschitz in $(u,p)$ on the common tube with constant $L_q$ in the sum norm, then
$$\|\nabla J_h-\nabla J\|_2\le\bigl(C_b+T(C_d+L_qC_x)+C_Q\bigr)h^p.$$
The adjoint, derivative-data and quadrature hypotheses are separate from state accuracy; without them the state estimate alone gives no gradient error conclusion.

There is also the following independent method-consistency conclusion. Under the local $C^1$ step-and-cost consistency, derivative stability, derivative Lipschitz, initial-data, terminal-derivative and tube hypotheses of [[lem-local-c1-step-consistency-implies-tangent-adjoint-gradient-order]], the actual numerical graph satisfies
$$\max_n\|D_\theta u_n-D_\theta u(t_n)\|_2\le C_Sh^p,\qquad \max_n\|p_n-p(t_n)\|_2\le C_Ph^p,$$
$$\|\nabla J_h-\nabla J\|_2\le C_Gh^p,$$
with that lemma's explicit constants, together with its state bound. These conclusions derive the global tangent and adjoint errors from local map errors. They do not assume the preceding global state/adjoint bound or weighted representation.

In particular, [[lem-explicit-rk-differentiated-stages-give-local-c1-order]] supplies these local hypotheses for the actual explicit RK state map and the cost using the same tableau, under its common-tube, base $C^2$, and local augmented-order hypotheses. For $p\le4$, its augmented $C^4$ hypothesis and the existing coefficient conditions suffice; jointly $C^5$ base data are an explicit sufficient smoothness condition, and its displayed classical RK4 tableau gives a concrete order-four instance. Generic $p$ is retained through its genuine local augmented-order hypothesis. This branch permits negative or zero RK weights and makes no internal-stage adjoint accuracy claim.

Assume Countable Choice and the elliptic state/adjoint setting of [[thm-elliptic-adjoint-reduced-gradient]]. Let $V_h\subseteq V$ be a finite-dimensional conforming space. Let $a_{\theta,h}$ and $\ell_{\theta,h}$ be operator-norm $C^1$ in $\theta$, uniformly coercive on $V_h$, and define the discrete state by $a_{\theta,h}(u_h,v_h)=\ell_{\theta,h}(v_h)$. Let $J_h:V_h\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, and let $p_h\in V_h$ solve $a_{\theta,h}(v_h,p_h)=D_uJ_h(u_h,\theta)[v_h]$. Suppose the parameter derivatives of the discrete forms and loads have specified bounded extensions to $V$ that agree with their values on $V_h$. Let $u,p$ be the exact state and adjoint, and let $u_h,p_h\in V_h$ be their discrete counterparts, with certified energy bounds
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le E_u,\qquad \|p-p_h\|_V\le E_p.$$
For an exact conforming Galerkin solve these bounds may be supplied by [[thm-cea-quasi-optimality-for-conforming-galerkin-approximations]]; for a conforming perturbed solve they may be supplied by [[thm-first-strang-lemma-for-conforming-perturbed-galerkin]], with all load, form, geometry and quadrature defects retained as in [[def-variational-crime-error-framework]]. Define exact and discrete reduced gradients by
$$g[\eta]=D_\theta J(u,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_\theta'[\eta](p)-a_\theta'[\eta](u,p),\qquad g_h[\eta]=D_\theta J_h(u_h,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta](p_h)-a_{\theta,h}'[\eta](u_h,p_h).$$
Assume for $\|\eta\|_2\le1$ that $\|\ell_\theta'[\eta]\|_{V^*}\le M_\ell$, $\|a_\theta'[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le M_a$, the direct-objective defect satisfies $|D_\theta J_h(u_h,\theta)[\eta]-D_\theta J(u,\theta)[\eta]|\le\varepsilon_J$, and the derivative-data defects obey
$$\|\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta]-\ell_\theta'[\eta]\|_{V^*}\le\varepsilon_\ell,\qquad \|a_{\theta,h}'[\eta]-a_\theta'[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le\varepsilon_a.$$
Put $U_*=\max(\|u\|_V,\|u_h\|_V)$ and $P_*=\max(\|p\|_V,\|p_h\|_V)$. Then
$$\|g_h-g\|_{\Theta^*}\le\varepsilon_J+M_\ell E_p+\varepsilon_\ell P_*+M_a(E_uP_*+U_*E_p)+\varepsilon_aU_*P_*.$$
The derivative-data defects are separate obligations: ordinary state and adjoint Strang bounds do not by themselves bound derivative defects.

Assume Countable Choice, and use the real evolution triple $(V,H,V^*)$ of [[def-parameterized-parabolic-variational-problem]]. On an open parameter set $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, assume the state map $\theta\mapsto u_\theta$ is Fr\'echet differentiable into $W(0,T;V)$, with derivative $w_\eta$ in direction $\eta\in\mathbb R^m$. Assume, for every $v\in V$ and almost every $t$,
$$\langle w_\eta'(t),v\rangle+a_\theta(t;w_\eta(t),v)=\langle f_\theta'[\eta](t),v\rangle-a_\theta'[\eta](t;u_\theta(t),v),\qquad w_\eta(0)=u_{0,\theta}'[\eta].$$
Let $\phi:H\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, and let $L:[0,T]\times V\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be measurable in time and $C^1$ in $(u,\theta)$ for almost every time, with a common integrable majorant that justifies differentiating its time integral. Assume $D_u\phi$ is represented by an element of $H$ and $D_uL(t,u_\theta,\theta)\in V^*$ is square-integrable in time. Suppose the adjoint $p\in W(0,T;V)$ satisfies
$$-\langle p'(t),v\rangle+a_\theta(t;v,p(t))=D_uL(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)[v],\qquad p(T)=\nabla_H\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta).$$
Then for $j(\theta)=\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)+\int_0^T L(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)\,dt$,
$$D j(\theta)[\eta]=D_\theta\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)[\eta]+(p(0),u_{0,\theta}'[\eta])_H+\int_0^T\left(D_\theta L(t,u_\theta,\theta)[\eta]+\langle f_\theta'[\eta](t),p(t)\rangle-a_\theta'[\eta](t;u_\theta(t),p(t))\right)dt.$$
This is conditional on the displayed differentiable state and adjoint; it does not prove either exists. The adjoint form is transposed as shown, so symmetry of $a_\theta$ is not required.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $A_1,\ldots,A_N\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be invertible, with $n,N\ge1$, and let $Q_0$ be orthogonal. For $1\le k\le N$, form the unique positive-diagonal QR factorization
$$A_kQ_{k-1}=Q_kR_k,$$
where $Q_k$ is orthogonal and $R_k$ is upper triangular with positive diagonal $r_{k,ii}$. Put $P_N=A_N\cdots A_1$ and define the exact finite-time log-volume change by $\log|\det P_N|$. Then
$$\log|\det P_N|=\sum_{k=1}^N\sum_{i=1}^n\log r_{k,ii}.$$
No infinite-time Lyapunov exponent or shadowing conclusion follows.

For a numerical log record, define $\sigma_{\min}(A):=\inf_{\|x\|_2=1}\|Ax\|_2$. If $\sigma_{\min}(A_k)\ge\sigma>0$, each exact $r_{k,ii}\ge\sigma$. If positive computed diagonals $\widetilde r_{k,ii}$ satisfy $|\widetilde r_{k,ii}-r_{k,ii}|\le\varepsilon_{k,i}\le\sigma/2$, and each computed logarithm $\widehat l_{k,i}$ satisfies $|\widehat l_{k,i}-\log\widetilde r_{k,ii}|\le\delta_{k,i}$, then
$$\left|\sum_{k,i}\widehat l_{k,i}-\log|\det P_N|\right|\le\sum_{k,i}\left(\frac{2\varepsilon_{k,i}}{\sigma}+\delta_{k,i}\right).$$
If any factor loses rank, this log-volume branch returns failure.
source_evidence.case_anchor: Invertible finite factors yield the exact log-volume identity and a conditioned log-record error bound; no infinite-time Lyapunov converse is claimed.

Let $s\ge1$, let $R_1,\ldots,R_s$ be complex matrices of one fixed shape,
and let $C\ge1$. Define
$$\mathcal C_{s,C}:=\{c\in\mathbb R^s:\sum_{i=1}^s c_i=1,\ \sum_{i=1}^s|c_i|\le C\}$$
and $J(c):=\|\sum_{i=1}^s c_iR_i\|_F^2$. Then $J$ attains a minimum on
$\mathcal C_{s,C}$. Among all minimizers there is a unique vector of minimum
Euclidean norm. This rule defines the exact capped DIIS coefficient vector even
when the least-squares Gram matrix is singular.
source_evidence.case_anchor: Capped DIIS least squares has a unique minimum-Euclidean-norm minimizer, even with singular Gram matrix; no converse characterization of residual matrices is asserted.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $H_0\in\mathbb H_n$ have eigenvalues with multiplicity
$\lambda_1(H_0)\le\cdots\le\lambda_n(H_0)$ and gap
$g=\lambda_{r+1}(H_0)-\lambda_r(H_0)>0$. Put
$$c=\lambda_1(H_0),\qquad R=\frac{\lambda_r(H_0)+\lambda_{r+1}(H_0)}2-c,$$
and let $\Gamma=\{c+Re^{it}:0\le t\le2\pi\}$ be positively oriented.
For Hermitian $H$, write $\sigma(H)=\{\lambda_j(H):1\le j\le n\}$.
Then
$R\ge g/2$. For every Hermitian $H$ with $\|H-H_0\|_{op}\le g/4$, exactly
the $r$ lowest eigenvalues of $H$, counted with multiplicity, lie inside $\Gamma$;
the gap is at least $g/2$, and
$$\operatorname{dist}(\Gamma,\sigma(H))\ge g/4,\qquad \|(zI-H)^{-1}\|_{op}\le4/g\quad(z\in\Gamma).$$
source_evidence.case_anchor: A positive occupied gap g and a perturbation of at most g/4 imply cluster separation and the resolvent bound4/g, without a converse perturbation threshold.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $H_0\in\mathbb H_n$ have an occupied/unoccupied gap
$g=\lambda_{r+1}(H_0)-\lambda_r(H_0)>0$, and let $c,R,\Gamma$ be the circle
from [[lem-spectral-gap-persistence-and-uniform-resolvent-bound]]. For Hermitian
$H$ in the open operator-norm ball $\|H-H_0\|_{op}<g/4$, let $\Pi_r(H)$ be its
projector onto the $r$ lowest eigenvalues. Then $H\mapsto\Pi_r(H)$ is real
Frechet $C^1$ in the Frobenius norm and
$$D\Pi_r(H)[E]=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma (zI-H)^{-1}E(zI-H)^{-1}\,dz$$
for each Hermitian direction $E$. With $\ell(\Gamma)=2\pi R$,
$$\|D\Pi_r(H)[E]\|_F\le\frac{16R}{g^2}\|E\|_F.$$
This is a block/cluster statement: no gap between eigenvalues inside either
cluster is required.
source_evidence.case_anchor: A strict occupied/virtual gap yields a C1 block-projector map and derivative estimate16R/g^2; no eigenvalue simplicity within a block is necessary.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $(K,d)$ be a nonempty complete metric space and let $\Phi:K\to K$ be a
contraction with constant $0\le q<1$. In the SCF application, $K$ is a
complete invariant subset of the response-map domain from
[[def-self-consistent-projector-response-map]], with $d(X,Y)=\|X-Y\|_F$.
Then $\Phi$ has a unique fixed point $X_*$ and exact iterates
$X_{k+1}=\Phi(X_k)$ satisfy
$$d(X_k,X_*)\le q^k d(X_0,X_*).$$
For every $X\in K$,
$$d(X,X_*)\le\frac{d(X,\Phi(X))}{1-q}.$$
If computed updates $X_{k+1}\in K$ obey
$d(X_{k+1},\Phi(X_k))\le\eta_k$, then
$$e_{k+1}\le q e_k+\eta_k,\qquad e_k\le q^k e_0+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q^{k-1-j}\eta_j,$$
where $e_k=d(X_k,X_*)$ and $X_0$ is the supplied initial point.
Use the convention $q^0=1$, including when $q=0$.
source_evidence.case_anchor: A contraction on a supplied nonempty complete invariant metric space gives fixed-point and residual/error estimates; a small residual alone is not asserted to imply contraction.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $K\subseteq U$ be a set of Hermitian inputs and suppose $F:K\to\mathbb H_n$ is
$L_F$-Lipschitz in Frobenius norm. Assume that for some Hermitian $H_0$ with
occupied gap $g>0$, every $F(X)$ lies in the open operator-norm ball of radius
$g/4$ about $H_0$. Use the common circle $\Gamma$ of
[[lem-spectral-gap-persistence-and-uniform-resolvent-bound]], with
$R=(\lambda_r(H_0)+\lambda_{r+1}(H_0))/2-\lambda_1(H_0)$. Then
$$\|\Phi(X)-\Phi(Y)\|_F\le q\|X-Y\|_F,\qquad q:=\frac{16R}{g^2}L_F.$$
Thus $q<1$ is a checkable contraction certificate when also $\Phi(K)\subseteq K$;
a positive gap by itself does not establish that inequality.
source_evidence.case_anchor: A common positive-gap contour and an LF-Lipschitz field yield q=16R LF/g^2, with invariance additionally required for a contraction; gap alone is not sufficient.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $K\subseteq\mathcal D_r$ be nonempty, closed, and convex in Frobenius norm.
Suppose $F$ is $C^1$ on an open neighborhood of $K$, every matrix $F(D)$ there
has a strict $r$th gap so the gapped projector map $\Phi$ is defined, and for a
fixed $\alpha\in[0,1]$ the relaxed map
$$T_\alpha(D)=(1-\alpha)D+\alpha\Phi(D)$$
satisfies $T_\alpha(K)\subseteq K$. If a certified induced-norm bound
$$\|DT_\alpha(D)\|_{F\to F}\le q\qquad(D\in K),\qquad 0\le q<1,$$
holds, where $\|A\|_{F\to F}:=\sup_{\|H\|_F=1}\|A[H]\|_F$, then
$T_\alpha$ is a contraction on $K$ and its iterates converge to a unique fixed
point. The derivative is
$$DT_\alpha(D)=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha D\Phi(D).$$
The derivative bound is a separate hypothesis; $\alpha>0$ alone does not imply
contraction.
source_evidence.case_anchor: An invariant relaxed response with an independently certified induced norm q<1 is contractive; positive mixing alpha alone is not a converse certificate.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume the hypotheses and certificates in
[[alg-certified-scf-with-diis-safeguard]]: $\Phi$ is a $q$-contraction on the
complete invariant set $K$, its fixed point is $P_*$, the starting error is at
most $E_0$, and every baseline response error is at most $\eta_k$. Let $E_k$
be updated by that algorithm. Then every produced iterate obeys
$$\|P_k-P_*\|_F\le E_k\le q^kE_0+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q^{k-1-j}\eta_j.$$
An accepted DIIS candidate has certified error at most $qE_k$; the commutator
least-squares residual alone is not used as an error bound. If the procedure is
continued indefinitely with successful certificates and $\eta_k\to0$, then
$P_k\to P_*$; a finite update cap still may return budget exhaustion.
Use the convention $q^0=1$, including when $q=0$.

Suppose the adjoint regularity and dual approximation assumptions of [[cor-aubin-nitsche-h-r-plus-s-rate-under-primal-and-dual-approximation]] hold separately for the state and adjoint equations, giving
$$\|u-u_h\|_{L^2}\le C_u h^{r+s},\qquad \|p-p_h\|_{L^2}\le C_p h^{r+s}$$
for $0<h\le1$, $r\ge1$, and $s\in(0,1]$. Assume the parameter derivative operators satisfy
$$|\ell_\theta'[\eta](v)|\le M_\ell^0\|\eta\|_2\|v\|_{L^2},\qquad |a_\theta'[\eta](v,w)|\le M_a^0\|\eta\|_2\|v\|_{L^2}\|w\|_{L^2}.$$
Assume the discrete derivative maps in [[thm-elliptic-fe-gradient-error-in-energy-norms]] have compatible $L^2$ extensions and constants $C_J,C_\ell,C_a$ independent of $h$ give, for every $\|\eta\|_2\le1$, a direct-objective derivative defect at most $C_Jh^{r+s}$, an $L^2$-dual load-derivative defect at most $C_\ell h^{r+s}$, and a bilinear derivative defect at most $C_ah^{r+s}\|v\|_{L^2}\|w\|_{L^2}$. Then the reduced-gradient error is $O(h^{r+s})$. This rate requires those extra $L^2$-bounded parameter derivative maps; the energy-norm result alone does not imply it.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice, and use the real evolution triple $(V,H,V^*)$ of [[def-parameterized-parabolic-variational-problem]]. On an open parameter set $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, assume the state map $\theta\mapsto u_\theta$ is Fr\'echet differentiable into $W(0,T;V)$, with derivative $w_\eta$ in direction $\eta\in\mathbb R^m$. Assume, for every $v\in V$ and almost every $t$,
$$\langle w_\eta'(t),v\rangle+a_\theta(t;w_\eta(t),v)=\langle f_\theta'[\eta](t),v\rangle-a_\theta'[\eta](t;u_\theta(t),v),\qquad w_\eta(0)=u_{0,\theta}'[\eta].$$
Let $\phi:H\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, and let $L:[0,T]\times V\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be measurable in time and $C^1$ in $(u,\theta)$ for almost every time, with a common integrable majorant that justifies differentiating its time integral. Assume $D_u\phi$ is represented by an element of $H$ and $D_uL(t,u_\theta,\theta)\in V^*$ is square-integrable in time. Suppose the adjoint $p\in W(0,T;V)$ satisfies
$$-\langle p'(t),v\rangle+a_\theta(t;v,p(t))=D_uL(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)[v],\qquad p(T)=\nabla_H\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta).$$
Then for $j(\theta)=\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)+\int_0^T L(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)\,dt$,
$$D j(\theta)[\eta]=D_\theta\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)[\eta]+(p(0),u_{0,\theta}'[\eta])_H+\int_0^T\left(D_\theta L(t,u_\theta,\theta)[\eta]+\langle f_\theta'[\eta](t),p(t)\rangle-a_\theta'[\eta](t;u_\theta(t),p(t))\right)dt.$$
This is conditional on the displayed differentiable state and adjoint; it does not prove either exists. The adjoint form is transposed as shown, so symmetry of $a_\theta$ is not required.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice and the differentiable state/adjoint setting of [[thm-parabolic-adjoint-gradient-sensitivity]]. Let $u,p$ and $u_h,p_h$ denote the continuous and semidiscrete state/adjoint pairs, with gradients $g,g_h$ given by that theorem and its finite-dimensional application. Assume $u,p\in H^1(0,T;V)$, the parabolic form and its parameter derivative are uniformly bounded, and the form is coercive with constant $\alpha>0$. Suppose the forward state and time-reversed adjoint both satisfy the hypotheses of [[thm-parabolic-semidiscrete-ritz-error-splitting-and-energy-bound]], with operator-norm $C^1$ comparison maps $P_{u,h}(t),P_{p,h}(t):V\to V_h$. For the state comparison map, set $\rho_u=P_{u,h}u-u$, $\vartheta_u=u_h-P_{u,h}u$, and
$$\mathcal R_u(t)(v_h)=(\rho_u'(t),v_h)_H+a_\theta(t;\rho_u(t),v_h),\qquad \rho_u'=P_{u,h}'(t)u+P_{u,h}(t)u'-u'.$$
In reverse time $s=T-t$, put $q(s)=p(T-s)$ and $\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)=P_{p,h}(T-s)$; define $\rho_p(s)=\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)-q(s)$, $\vartheta_p(s)=p_h(T-s)-\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)$, and $\mathcal R_p(s)(v_h)=(\rho_p'(s),v_h)_H+a_\theta(T-s;v_h,\rho_p(s))$. The projection product rule gives $\rho_p'=\widetilde P_{p,h}'q+\widetilde P_{p,h}q'-q'$, with $\widetilde P_{p,h}'(s)=-P_{p,h}'(T-s)$. The Ritz supplier gives, for $z=u,p$,
$$\|z-z_h\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}\le E_z:=\|\rho_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}+\alpha^{-1/2}\left(\|\vartheta_z(0)\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|\mathcal R_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2\right)^{1/2},$$
where the adjoint's initial trace means its terminal trace in original time. In particular, $\mathcal R_z$ contains the derivative of the time-dependent projection; it cannot be dropped from this hypothesis.

For $\|\eta\|_2\le1$, assume $\|D_\theta f[\eta]\|_{L^2(V^*)}\le M_f$, $\|D_\theta a(t)[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le M_a$ a.e., and define $U_*:=\max(\|u\|_{L^2(V)},\|u_h\|_{L^2(V)})$, $P_*:=\max(\|p\|_{L^2(V)},\|p_h\|_{L^2(V)})$, $P_{0,*}:=\max(\|p(0)\|_H,\|p_h(0)\|_H)$, and $U_0':=\|D_\theta u_0\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,H)}$. Suppose the discrete direct-objective derivative differs from the continuous direct-objective derivative $D_\theta\phi+\int_0^T D_\theta L\,dt$ by at most $\varepsilon_J$ in $\Theta^*$; suppose also $\|D_\theta u_{0,h}-D_\theta u_0\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,H)}\le\varepsilon_0$, $\|D_\theta f_h-D_\theta f\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,L^2(V^*))}\le\varepsilon_f$, and $\|D_\theta a_h-D_\theta a\|_{L^\infty(0,T;\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,\mathcal L(V,V^*)))}\le\varepsilon_a$. Put $E_{p,0}=\|p_h(0)-p(0)\|_H$. Then
$$\|g_h-g\|_{(\mathbb R^m)^*}\le \varepsilon_J+U_0'E_{p,0}+P_{0,*}\varepsilon_0+M_fE_p+\varepsilon_fP_*+M_a(E_uP_*+U_*E_p)+\varepsilon_aU_*P_*.$$
The derivative-data and trace defects are additional assumptions; an energy estimate for the state alone does not imply this gradient bound.

source_evidence.fullclaim: Let $V=H_0^1(0,1)$ with its standard $H^1$ norm, let $\Theta=(-1,\infty)$, and define $a_\theta(u,v)=(1+\theta)\int_0^1u'v'\,dx$ and $\ell(v)=\int_0^1v\,dx$. Take $J(u)=\int_0^1u\,dx$. On a neighborhood of each fixed $\theta>-1$, the form is uniformly coercive in the $H^1$ norm, so this is a parameterized coercive elliptic problem in the sense of [[def-parameterized-elliptic-variational-problem]].

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: Put $w(x)=x(1-x)/2$. Direct differentiation gives $w''=-1$, $w(0)=w(1)=0$, and [F3] gives $w\in V$. For each $v\in V$ and $\varepsilon>0$, [F5] supplies $v_\varepsilon\in C_c^\infty(0,1)$ with $\|v-v_\varepsilon\|_{H^1}<\varepsilon$. By the product rule [F7], $(w'v_\varepsilon)'=w''v_\varepsilon+w'v_\varepsilon'$; since $v_\varepsilon$ vanishes at both endpoints, [F6] gives $\int_0^1w'v_\varepsilon'=\int_0^1v_\varepsilon$. By [F8], the difference between the two sides with $v$ in place of $v_\varepsilon$ is at most $(\|w'\|_{L^2}+1)\varepsilon$, so the weak identity $\int_0^1w'v'=\int_0^1v$ follows as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. Also, [F4] gives $a_\theta(v,v)\ge(1+\theta)\|v\|_{H^1}^2/2$; on a neighborhood of each $\theta>-1$ this is a uniform coercivity bound. Hence $u_\theta=w/(1+\theta)$ solves the state equation and is unique. Finally $\int_0^1w=1/12$, so $j(\theta)=1/(12(1+\theta))$. [A1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, given, algebra]

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $N\ge1$, and for $0\le n\le N$ let $U_n\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_n}$ be open. A finite parameterized state-step graph consists of a $C^1$ initial map $x_0:\Theta\to U_0$ and $C^1$ step maps $\Psi_n:U_n\times\Theta\to U_{n+1}$ for $0\le n<N$, such that the recursion $x_{n+1}(\theta)=\Psi_n(x_n(\theta),\theta)$ is defined for every $\theta$ in the chosen parameter neighborhood. A $C^1$ running objective consists of maps $\ell_n:U_n\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ and a terminal objective $\phi:U_N\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$, all $C^1$. Its reduced objective is
$$J(\theta)=\phi(x_N(\theta),\theta)+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\ell_n(x_n(\theta),\theta).$$
The maps and objective define one finite real-arithmetic graph. A gradient of this graph is the derivative of this finite composition; it is not the derivative of an exact implicit solution unless the step map itself is that solution map.

source_evidence.fullclaim: Let $V$ be a real Hilbert space, let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and write $V^*$ for the continuous real dual. A parameter-dependent coercive elliptic variational problem is a family of bounded bilinear forms $a_\theta:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ and bounded linear functionals $\ell_\theta\in V^*$ such that, on each parameter neighborhood under discussion, $\|a_\theta\|\le M$ and $a_\theta(v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2$ for fixed $M<\infty$ and $\alpha>0$. Operator-norm $C^1$ data means that the maps $\theta\mapsto A_\theta\in\mathcal L(V,V^*)$, $A_\theta u:=a_\theta(u,\cdot)$, and $\theta\mapsto\ell_\theta\in V^*$ are continuously Fréchet differentiable. A state at $\theta$ is a vector $u_\theta\in V$ satisfying $a_\theta(u_\theta,v)=\ell_\theta(v)$ for every $v\in V$. When a state is specified, a $C^1$ objective $J:V\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ defines the reduced objective $j(\theta)=J(u_\theta,\theta)$. This definition alone asserts neither state existence nor uniqueness of an optimizer.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ and $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d\times\Theta$ be open, and let $f:D\to\mathbb R^d$ be continuously differentiable. Let $V_\theta\subseteq\Theta$ be open and $u_0:V_\theta\to\mathbb R^d$ be $C^1$. Assume there is a bounded convex open set $O\subset D$ with compact closure in $D$ such that for every $\theta\in V_\theta$ the unique solution of $u'=f(t,u,\theta)$, $u(0)=u_0(\theta)$, exists on $[0,T]$, and all triples $(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)$ lie in $O$. Then $\theta\mapsto u_\theta$ is $C^1$ as a map to $C([0,T];\mathbb R^d)$. For any $\theta_0\in V_\theta$, its tangent matrix $S(t)=D_\theta u_\theta(t)|_{\theta=\theta_0}$ is the unique solution of
$$S'(t)=D_u f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0)S(t)+D_\theta f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0),\qquad S(0)=D u_0(\theta_0).$$
The result is local to the stated common compact tube and claims no differentiability outside it.

actualproofparagraphs.2.1: Put $A(t)=D_u f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0)$ and $B(t)=D_\theta f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0)$, and define $\rho_h(t)=f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t)+\delta_h(t),\theta_0+h)-f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0)-A(t)\delta_h(t)-B(t)h$. Uniform continuity of $D f$ on $\overline O$ and the integral remainder along the secant give $\sup_t\|\rho_h(t)\|_2=o(\|h\|_2)$, since step 1.1 gives $\sup_t(\|\delta_h(t)\|_2+\|h\|_2)=O(\|h\|_2)$. Also $u_0(\theta_0+h)-u_0(\theta_0)=D u_0(\theta_0)h+o(\|h\|_2)$. [A1, step 1.1]
actualproofparagraphs.3.1: Let $E_h(t)=\delta_h(t)-S(t)h$, and let $r_0(h)=u_0(\theta_0+h)-u_0(\theta_0)-D u_0(\theta_0)h$. The Volterra equations and the field remainder $\rho_h$ from step 2.1 give $E_h(t)=r_0(h)+\int_0^t\bigl(A(s)E_h(s)+\rho_h(s)\bigr)ds$, where $A(s)=D_u f(s,u_{\theta_0}(s),\theta_0)$. By [F4], $\|E_h(t)\|_2\le\|r_0(h)\|_2+T\sup_s\|\rho_h(s)\|_2+L\int_0^t\|E_h(s)\|_2ds$. Both first terms are $o(\|h\|_2)$ by step 2.1 and differentiability of $u_0$. Applying [F3] yields $\sup_t\|E_h(t)\|_2=o(\|h\|_2)$. Thus the Fréchet derivative at $\theta_0$ exists and equals $S$. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.2, step 2.1]

Let $S\in C^1([0,T];\mathbb R^{d\times m})$ and $p\in C^1([0,T];\mathbb R^d)$ satisfy $S'=A S+B$ and $p'=-A^T p-g$, where $A,B,g$ are continuous and have compatible dimensions. Then
$$p(T)^T S(T)-p(0)^T S(0)=\int_0^T\bigl(-g(t)^T S(t)+p(t)^T B(t)\bigr)\,dt.$$

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: Write $p^T S=\sum_{i=1}^d p_i S_{i,\cdot}$. By [F2] coordinatewise, $(p^TS)'=(p')^TS+p^TS'$. Substituting the two equations yields $(-A^Tp-g)^TS+p^T(AS+B)=-g^TS+p^TB$, because $(A^Tp)^TS=p^TAS$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]
actualproofparagraphs.2.1: The right-hand side in step 1.1 is continuous and hence integrable. Apply [F3] to the scalar function $p^TS$ and integrate step 1.1 over $[0,T]$. This gives the stated endpoint identity. [F3, step 1.1] ∎

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Use the setting of [[def-parameterized-finite-state-step-objective]]. Write $A_n=D_x\Psi_n(x_n,\theta)$, $B_n=D_\theta\Psi_n(x_n,\theta)$, and let $S_n=D_\theta x_n$. Then
$$S_0=D x_0(\theta),\qquad S_{n+1}=A_nS_n+B_n.$$
Define $p_N=D_x\phi(x_N,\theta)^T$ and, backward for $n=N-1,\ldots,0$,
$$p_n=D_x\ell_n(x_n,\theta)^T+A_n^Tp_{n+1}.$$
The exact gradient of the finite objective is
$$\nabla_\theta J=D_\theta\phi(x_N,\theta)^T+S_0^Tp_0+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\bigl(D_\theta\ell_n(x_n,\theta)^T+B_n^Tp_{n+1}\bigr).$$
The recursion is the reverse derivative of the finite graph in exact real arithmetic; it makes no convergence claim about an iteration used to choose $\theta$.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: By the chain rule [F4] applied to $x_{n+1}(\theta)=\Psi_n(x_n(\theta),\theta)$, $S_{n+1}=A_nS_n+B_n$; differentiating the initial map gives $S_0=Dx_0(\theta)$. These are the forward tangent equations for this finite composition. [F1, F4]
actualproofparagraphs.3.1: The adjoint equation gives $p_n^TS_n=D_x\ell_nS_n+p_{n+1}^TA_nS_n$. Since $S_{n+1}=A_nS_n+B_n$, rearranging yields $$D_x\ell_nS_n=p_n^TS_n-p_{n+1}^TS_{n+1}+p_{n+1}^TB_n.$$ Summing over $n$ telescopes; $p_N=D_x\phi^T$ cancels the terminal tangent term in step 2.1 and leaves $S_0^Tp_0+\sum_n B_n^Tp_{n+1}$. Adding the direct parameter derivatives from step 2.1 gives the displayed adjoint formula. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $u_\theta$ solve the parameter-dependent ODE of [[lem-parameter-ode-flow-tangent-on-common-tube]] on $[0,T]$. Let
$$J(\theta)=\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)+\int_0^T\ell(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)\,dt,$$
where $\phi$ and $\ell$ are $C^1$ on a neighborhood of the trajectory tube and their first derivatives are bounded and uniformly continuous there. Let $S=D_\theta u_\theta$ be the tangent from that lemma. Let $p$ solve the terminal adjoint problem
$$-p'(t)=D_u f(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)^Tp(t)+D_u\ell(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)^T,\qquad p(T)=D_u\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)^T.$$
Then
$$\nabla_\theta J=D_\theta\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)^T+D_\theta u_0(\theta)^Tp(0)+\int_0^T\bigl(D_\theta\ell(t,u_\theta,\theta)^T+D_\theta f(t,u_\theta,\theta)^Tp(t)\bigr)\,dt.$$
This formula separates initial, terminal, running-cost and vector-field parameter terms. It applies only while the common-tube and differentiability hypotheses hold.

actualproofparagraphs.1.3: In [F2], set $A=D_uf$, $B=D_\theta f$, and $g=D_u\ell^T$. The adjoint equation in the Statement and tangent equation in [F1] satisfy its hypotheses. source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $J$ and $J_h$ be the continuous and finite state-step objectives of [[thm-continuous-ode-adjoint-gradient-formula]] and [[thm-discrete-adjoint-gradient-recursion]], respectively, and put $h=T/N$. Let $q(t,u,p)=D_\theta\ell(t,u,\theta)^T+D_\theta f(t,u,\theta)^Tp$ be the continuous running-gradient vector, evaluated on its exact state and adjoint as $q(t):=q(t,u(t),p(t))$. Suppose the exact and numerical state/adjoint pairs lie in a common tube and
$$\max_n\bigl(\|u_n-u(t_n)\|_2+\|p_n-p(t_n)\|_2\bigr)\le C_xh^p.$$
For the state part of this bound, it is sufficient that the hypotheses of [[thm-global-error-from-one-step-defect-and-stability]] hold with a uniform $O(h^{p+1})$ exact-start defect; the coefficient conditions of [[prop-explicit-rk-order-conditions-through-four]] supply that defect for an explicit Runge--Kutta method of order $p\le4$ under that item's $C^4$ and common-tube assumptions. No cited state-error result supplies the adjoint part, which is an independent hypothesis here. Write $b$ and $b_h$ for the column initial/terminal contribution vectors in the continuous and discrete gradient formulas. Assume the discrete running-gradient terms admit vectors $\widehat q_n$ and nonnegative weights $w_n$, $0\le n\le N$, with
$$\nabla J_h=b_h+\sum_{n=0}^N w_n\widehat q_n,\qquad \nabla J=b+\int_0^Tq(t)\,dt,\qquad \sum_{n=0}^Nw_n=T.$$
The weighted discrete representation is an explicit premise; it is not implied by the generic finite state-step adjoint recursion. Suppose
$$\|\widehat q_n-q(t_n,u_n,p_n)\|_2\le C_dh^p,\qquad \|b_h-b\|_2\le C_bh^p,$$
and that the same weights give the quadrature $Q_h(q)=\sum_{n=0}^Nw_nq(t_n)$ satisfying
$$\left\|Q_h(q)-\int_0^Tq(t)\,dt\right\|_2\le C_Qh^p.$$
If $q$ is Lipschitz in $(u,p)$ on the common tube with constant $L_q$ in the sum norm, then
$$\|\nabla J_h-\nabla J\|_2\le\bigl(C_b+T(C_d+L_qC_x)+C_Q\bigr)h^p.$$
The adjoint, derivative-data and quadrature hypotheses are separate from state accuracy; without them the state estimate alone gives no gradient error conclusion.

There is also the following independent method-consistency conclusion. Under the local $C^1$ step-and-cost consistency, derivative stability, derivative Lipschitz, initial-data, terminal-derivative and tube hypotheses of [[lem-local-c1-step-consistency-implies-tangent-adjoint-gradient-order]], the actual numerical graph satisfies
$$\max_n\|D_\theta u_n-D_\theta u(t_n)\|_2\le C_Sh^p,\qquad \max_n\|p_n-p(t_n)\|_2\le C_Ph^p,$$
$$\|\nabla J_h-\nabla J\|_2\le C_Gh^p,$$
with that lemma's explicit constants, together with its state bound. These conclusions derive the global tangent and adjoint errors from local map errors. They do not assume the preceding global state/adjoint bound or weighted representation.

In particular, [[lem-explicit-rk-differentiated-stages-give-local-c1-order]] supplies these local hypotheses for the actual explicit RK state map and the cost using the same tableau, under its common-tube, base $C^2$, and local augmented-order hypotheses. For $p\le4$, its augmented $C^4$ hypothesis and the existing coefficient conditions suffice; jointly $C^5$ base data are an explicit sufficient smoothness condition, and its displayed classical RK4 tableau gives a concrete order-four instance. Generic $p$ is retained through its genuine local augmented-order hypothesis. This branch permits negative or zero RK weights and makes no internal-stage adjoint accuracy claim.

actualproofparagraphs.1.2: Independently assume [A2]. Apply [F5] to the actual maps defining $J_h$ and the exact interval flow and running-cost maps defining $J$. Its forward recurrences give state and tangent errors, its backward recurrence gives the nodal-adjoint error, and its graph-gradient comparison gives the stated $C_Gh^p$ bound. This argument uses no weighted decomposition. [A2, F5]
actualproofparagraphs.4.1: For the RK specialization, [F6] differentiates the actual finite stages, proves the local derivative-size and Lipschitz bounds, and obtains the needed local $C^1$ consistency from augmented local order. Its application of [F4] to the augmented field verifies this order for $p\le4$ under the actual augmented smoothness and tube assumptions. Its RK4 coefficient calculation supplies the concrete fourth-order instance. Therefore step 1.2 applies. [A2, F4, F6, step 1.2] ∎

Let $u=u(\theta)$ be $C^1$ and consider a selected $s$-stage Runge–Kutta branch for a $C^1$ parameter-dependent vector field $f(t,y,\theta)$. Let $F(Y,u,\theta)$ be the stack of its stage evaluations and
$$G(Y,u,\theta)=Y-\mathbf1\otimes u-h(A\otimes I_d)F(Y,u,\theta).$$
Assume the branch is the unique root in the invariant ball of [[lem-small-step-implicit-rk-branch-and-residual-error]], and its stage derivative $G_Y$ obeys the hypotheses of [[lem-implicit-rk-stage-jacobian-nonsingular-on-branch]]. Then the branch $Y(\theta)$ is locally $C^1$ and
$$D_\theta Y=-G_Y^{-1}\bigl(G_uD_\theta u+G_\theta\bigr).$$
For the update $\Psi_h(u,\theta)=u+h(\mathbf1^T_b\otimes I_d)F(Y(\theta),u(\theta),\theta)$,
$$D_\theta\Psi_h=D_\theta u+h(b^T\otimes I_d)\bigl(F_YD_\theta Y+F_uD_\theta u+F_\theta\bigr).$$
These are exact derivatives of the selected algebraic stage branch. A finite-budget stage iteration is a different map and is not covered by this formula.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice and the setting of [[def-parameterized-elliptic-variational-problem]]. On an open neighborhood $\Theta_0\subseteq\Theta$, suppose the same constants $M<\infty$ and $\alpha>0$ give boundedness and coercivity for every $a_\theta$, and $\theta\mapsto A_\theta$ and $\theta\mapsto\ell_\theta$ are operator-norm $C^1$. Then each state $u_\theta$ exists uniquely, the map $\theta\mapsto u_\theta\in V$ is $C^1$, and for each direction $\eta\in\mathbb R^m$ its derivative $w_\eta=D_\theta u_\theta[\eta]$ is the unique solution of
$$a_\theta(w_\eta,v)=D_\theta\ell_\theta[\eta](v)-D_\theta a_\theta[\eta](u_\theta,v)\qquad(v\in V).$$
Uniform coercivity is required on the parameter neighborhood; no differentiability conclusion is asserted at a loss of coercivity.

actualproofparagraphs.2.1: For sufficiently small $h$ with $\theta+h\in\Theta_0$, put $\delta u=u_{\theta+h}-u_\theta$, $\delta A=A_{\theta+h}-A_\theta$, and $\delta\ell=\ell_{\theta+h}-\ell_\theta$. Subtract the two variational equations to get $a_\theta(\delta u,v)=\delta\ell(v)-(\delta A\,u_{\theta+h})(v)$. Taking $v=\delta u$, using coercivity and the dual norm, and dividing by $\|\delta u\|_V$ when it is nonzero gives $\|\delta u\|_V\le\alpha^{-1}\bigl(\|\delta\ell\|_{V^*}+\|\delta A\|\,\|u_{\theta+h}\|_V\bigr)=O(\|h\|_2)$. The same bound is immediate when $\delta u=0$. Thus the state map is locally Lipschitz. [A1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]
actualproofparagraphs.2.2: For each direction $h\in\mathbb R^m$, define $w_h$ by $a_\theta(w_h,v)=D\ell_\theta[h](v)-\bigl(DA_\theta[h]u_\theta\bigr)(v)$. The right side is a bounded linear functional, so [F1] gives a unique $w_h$. Uniqueness and linearity of the right side in $h$ show $h\mapsto w_h$ is linear. [F1, F2, step 1.1, given]

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice and the elliptic state/adjoint setting of [[thm-elliptic-adjoint-reduced-gradient]]. Let $V_h\subseteq V$ be a finite-dimensional conforming space. Let $a_{\theta,h}$ and $\ell_{\theta,h}$ be operator-norm $C^1$ in $\theta$, uniformly coercive on $V_h$, and define the discrete state by $a_{\theta,h}(u_h,v_h)=\ell_{\theta,h}(v_h)$. Let $J_h:V_h\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, and let $p_h\in V_h$ solve $a_{\theta,h}(v_h,p_h)=D_uJ_h(u_h,\theta)[v_h]$. Suppose the parameter derivatives of the discrete forms and loads have specified bounded extensions to $V$ that agree with their values on $V_h$. Let $u,p$ be the exact state and adjoint, and let $u_h,p_h\in V_h$ be their discrete counterparts, with certified energy bounds
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le E_u,\qquad \|p-p_h\|_V\le E_p.$$
For an exact conforming Galerkin solve these bounds may be supplied by [[thm-cea-quasi-optimality-for-conforming-galerkin-approximations]]; for a conforming perturbed solve they may be supplied by [[thm-first-strang-lemma-for-conforming-perturbed-galerkin]], with all load, form, geometry and quadrature defects retained as in [[def-variational-crime-error-framework]]. Define exact and discrete reduced gradients by
$$g[\eta]=D_\theta J(u,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_\theta'[\eta](p)-a_\theta'[\eta](u,p),\qquad g_h[\eta]=D_\theta J_h(u_h,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta](p_h)-a_{\theta,h}'[\eta](u_h,p_h).$$
Assume for $\|\eta\|_2\le1$ that $\|\ell_\theta'[\eta]\|_{V^*}\le M_\ell$, $\|a_\theta'[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le M_a$, the direct-objective defect satisfies $|D_\theta J_h(u_h,\theta)[\eta]-D_\theta J(u,\theta)[\eta]|\le\varepsilon_J$, and the derivative-data defects obey
$$\|\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta]-\ell_\theta'[\eta]\|_{V^*}\le\varepsilon_\ell,\qquad \|a_{\theta,h}'[\eta]-a_\theta'[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le\varepsilon_a.$$
Put $U_*=\max(\|u\|_V,\|u_h\|_V)$ and $P_*=\max(\|p\|_V,\|p_h\|_V)$. Then
$$\|g_h-g\|_{\Theta^*}\le\varepsilon_J+M_\ell E_p+\varepsilon_\ell P_*+M_a(E_uP_*+U_*E_p)+\varepsilon_aU_*P_*.$$
The derivative-data defects are separate obligations: ordinary state and adjoint Strang bounds do not by themselves bound derivative defects.

actualproofparagraphs.2.1: Fix $\eta$ with $\|\eta\|_2\le1$. Subtract the continuous and discrete formulas. The direct-objective term is bounded by $\varepsilon_J$. Add and subtract $\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta](p_h)$; the load-derivative difference is at most $\varepsilon_\ell P_*+M_\ell E_p$. [F1, step 1.2, given, algebra]
actualproofparagraphs.4.1: Taking the supremum over all $\|\eta\|_2\le1$ gives the asserted dual norm bound. The separate $\varepsilon$ terms show why state error alone does not certify a reduced-gradient error. [step 3.1, algebra] ∎

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice, and use the real evolution triple $(V,H,V^*)$ of [[def-parameterized-parabolic-variational-problem]]. On an open parameter set $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, assume the state map $\theta\mapsto u_\theta$ is Fr\'echet differentiable into $W(0,T;V)$, with derivative $w_\eta$ in direction $\eta\in\mathbb R^m$. Assume, for every $v\in V$ and almost every $t$,
$$\langle w_\eta'(t),v\rangle+a_\theta(t;w_\eta(t),v)=\langle f_\theta'[\eta](t),v\rangle-a_\theta'[\eta](t;u_\theta(t),v),\qquad w_\eta(0)=u_{0,\theta}'[\eta].$$
Let $\phi:H\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, and let $L:[0,T]\times V\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be measurable in time and $C^1$ in $(u,\theta)$ for almost every time, with a common integrable majorant that justifies differentiating its time integral. Assume $D_u\phi$ is represented by an element of $H$ and $D_uL(t,u_\theta,\theta)\in V^*$ is square-integrable in time. Suppose the adjoint $p\in W(0,T;V)$ satisfies
$$-\langle p'(t),v\rangle+a_\theta(t;v,p(t))=D_uL(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)[v],\qquad p(T)=\nabla_H\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta).$$
Then for $j(\theta)=\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)+\int_0^T L(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)\,dt$,
$$D j(\theta)[\eta]=D_\theta\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)[\eta]+(p(0),u_{0,\theta}'[\eta])_H+\int_0^T\left(D_\theta L(t,u_\theta,\theta)[\eta]+\langle f_\theta'[\eta](t),p(t)\rangle-a_\theta'[\eta](t;u_\theta(t),p(t))\right)dt.$$

Assume Countable Choice and the differentiable state/adjoint setting of [[thm-parabolic-adjoint-gradient-sensitivity]]. Let $u,p$ and $u_h,p_h$ denote the continuous and semidiscrete state/adjoint pairs, with gradients $g,g_h$ given by that theorem and its finite-dimensional application. Assume $u,p\in H^1(0,T;V)$, the parabolic form and its parameter derivative are uniformly bounded, and the form is coercive with constant $\alpha>0$. Suppose the forward state and time-reversed adjoint both satisfy the hypotheses of [[thm-parabolic-semidiscrete-ritz-error-splitting-and-energy-bound]], with operator-norm $C^1$ comparison maps $P_{u,h}(t),P_{p,h}(t):V\to V_h$. For the state comparison map, set $\rho_u=P_{u,h}u-u$, $\vartheta_u=u_h-P_{u,h}u$, and
$$\mathcal R_u(t)(v_h)=(\rho_u'(t),v_h)_H+a_\theta(t;\rho_u(t),v_h),\qquad \rho_u'=P_{u,h}'(t)u+P_{u,h}(t)u'-u'.$$
In reverse time $s=T-t$, put $q(s)=p(T-s)$ and $\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)=P_{p,h}(T-s)$; define $\rho_p(s)=\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)-q(s)$, $\vartheta_p(s)=p_h(T-s)-\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)$, and $\mathcal R_p(s)(v_h)=(\rho_p'(s),v_h)_H+a_\theta(T-s;v_h,\rho_p(s))$. The projection product rule gives $\rho_p'=\widetilde P_{p,h}'q+\widetilde P_{p,h}q'-q'$, with $\widetilde P_{p,h}'(s)=-P_{p,h}'(T-s)$. The Ritz supplier gives, for $z=u,p$,
$$\|z-z_h\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}\le E_z:=\|\rho_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}+\alpha^{-1/2}\left(\|\vartheta_z(0)\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|\mathcal R_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2\right)^{1/2},$$
where the adjoint's initial trace means its terminal trace in original time. In particular, $\mathcal R_z$ contains the derivative of the time-dependent projection; it cannot be dropped from this hypothesis.

For $\|\eta\|_2\le1$, assume $\|D_\theta f[\eta]\|_{L^2(V^*)}\le M_f$, $\|D_\theta a(t)[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le M_a$ a.e., and define $U_*:=\max(\|u\|_{L^2(V)},\|u_h\|_{L^2(V)})$, $P_*:=\max(\|p\|_{L^2(V)},\|p_h\|_{L^2(V)})$, $P_{0,*}:=\max(\|p(0)\|_H,\|p_h(0)\|_H)$, and $U_0':=\|D_\theta u_0\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,H)}$. Suppose the discrete direct-objective derivative differs from the continuous direct-objective derivative $D_\theta\phi+\int_0^T D_\theta L\,dt$ by at most $\varepsilon_J$ in $\Theta^*$; suppose also $\|D_\theta u_{0,h}-D_\theta u_0\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,H)}\le\varepsilon_0$, $\|D_\theta f_h-D_\theta f\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,L^2(V^*))}\le\varepsilon_f$, and $\|D_\theta a_h-D_\theta a\|_{L^\infty(0,T;\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,\mathcal L(V,V^*)))}\le\varepsilon_a$. Put $E_{p,0}=\|p_h(0)-p(0)\|_H$. Then
$$\|g_h-g\|_{(\mathbb R^m)^*}\le \varepsilon_J+U_0'E_{p,0}+P_{0,*}\varepsilon_0+M_fE_p+\varepsilon_fP_*+M_a(E_uP_*+U_*E_p)+\varepsilon_aU_*P_*.$$
The derivative-data and trace defects are additional assumptions; an energy estimate for the state alone does not imply this gradient bound.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $A_1,\ldots,A_N\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be invertible, with $n,N\ge1$, and let $Q_0$ be orthogonal. For $1\le k\le N$, form the unique positive-diagonal QR factorization
$$A_kQ_{k-1}=Q_kR_k,$$
where $Q_k$ is orthogonal and $R_k$ is upper triangular with positive diagonal $r_{k,ii}$. Put $P_N=A_N\cdots A_1$ and define the exact finite-time log-volume change by $\log|\det P_N|$. Then
$$\log|\det P_N|=\sum_{k=1}^N\sum_{i=1}^n\log r_{k,ii}.$$
No infinite-time Lyapunov exponent or shadowing conclusion follows.

For a numerical log record, define $\sigma_{\min}(A):=\inf_{\|x\|_2=1}\|Ax\|_2$. If $\sigma_{\min}(A_k)\ge\sigma>0$, each exact $r_{k,ii}\ge\sigma$. If positive computed diagonals $\widetilde r_{k,ii}$ satisfy $|\widetilde r_{k,ii}-r_{k,ii}|\le\varepsilon_{k,i}\le\sigma/2$, and each computed logarithm $\widehat l_{k,i}$ satisfies $|\widehat l_{k,i}-\log\widetilde r_{k,ii}|\le\delta_{k,i}$, then
$$\left|\sum_{k,i}\widehat l_{k,i}-\log|\det P_N|\right|\le\sum_{k,i}\left(\frac{2\varepsilon_{k,i}}{\sigma}+\delta_{k,i}\right).$$
If any factor loses rank, this log-volume branch returns failure.

actualproofparagraphs.3.1: Both $r_{k,ii}$ and $\widetilde r_{k,ii}$ are at least $\sigma/2$. By [F5], $|\log\widetilde r_{k,ii}-\log r_{k,ii}|\le(2/\sigma)|\widetilde r_{k,ii}-r_{k,ii}|$. Adding the computation error $\delta_{k,i}$ and summing the scalar bounds by the triangle inequality proves the stated numerical log bound. The lower singular-value bound is essential to keep the log derivative bounded; if any factor is singular its determinant is zero and its log-volume is undefined. [A1, F5, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

$$J(\theta)=\phi(x_N(\theta),\theta)+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\ell_n(x_n(\theta),\theta).$$
The maps and objective define one finite real-arithmetic graph. A gradient of this graph is the derivative of this finite composition; it is not the derivative of an exact implicit solution unless the step map itself is that solution map.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ and $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d\times\Theta$ be open, and let $f:D\to\mathbb R^d$ be continuously differentiable. Let $V_\theta\subseteq\Theta$ be open and $u_0:V_\theta\to\mathbb R^d$ be $C^1$. Assume there is a bounded convex open set $O\subset D$ with compact closure in $D$ such that for every $\theta\in V_\theta$ the unique solution of $u'=f(t,u,\theta)$, $u(0)=u_0(\theta)$, exists on $[0,T]$, and all triples $(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)$ lie in $O$. Then $\theta\mapsto u_\theta$ is $C^1$ as a map to $C([0,T];\mathbb R^d)$. For any $\theta_0\in V_\theta$, its tangent matrix $S(t)=D_\theta u_\theta(t)|_{\theta=\theta_0}$ is the unique solution of
$$S'(t)=D_u f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0)S(t)+D_\theta f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0),\qquad S(0)=D u_0(\theta_0).$$
The result is local to the stated common compact tube and claims no differentiability outside it.

actualproofparagraphs.1.2: Put $A(t)=D_u f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0)$ and let $B_j(t)$ be column $j$ of $D_\theta f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0)$. For each parameter coordinate $j$, the augmented vector $Z_j=(S_{\cdot j},1)$ solves the homogeneous linear system $$Z_j'(t)=\begin{pmatrix}A(t)&B_j(t)\\0&0\end{pmatrix}Z_j(t),\qquad Z_j(0)=\begin{pmatrix}D u_0(\theta_0)_{\cdot j}\\1\end{pmatrix}.$$ Embed $Z_j(0)$ as one column of a square $(d+1)\times(d+1)$ initial matrix, with all other columns zero. The unique linear matrix solution supplied by [F5] has that vector solution as the selected column. Thus the tangent equation has a unique solution for each of the finitely many columns. [A1, F5, construct]

$$S_0=D x_0(\theta),\qquad S_{n+1}=A_nS_n+B_n.$$
Define $p_N=D_x\phi(x_N,\theta)^T$ and, backward for $n=N-1,\ldots,0$,
$$p_n=D_x\ell_n(x_n,\theta)^T+A_n^Tp_{n+1}.$$
The exact gradient of the finite objective is
$$\nabla_\theta J=D_\theta\phi(x_N,\theta)^T+S_0^Tp_0+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\bigl(D_\theta\ell_n(x_n,\theta)^T+B_n^Tp_{n+1}\bigr).$$

actualproofparagraphs.1.2: Apply the reverse accumulation rule [F2] to the finite graph of states and objective summands in [F1]. Let $J$ and $J_h$ be the continuous and finite state-step objectives of [[thm-continuous-ode-adjoint-gradient-formula]] and [[thm-discrete-adjoint-gradient-recursion]], respectively, and put $h=T/N$. Let $q(t,u,p)=D_\theta\ell(t,u,\theta)^T+D_\theta f(t,u,\theta)^Tp$ be the continuous running-gradient vector, evaluated on its exact state and adjoint as $q(t):=q(t,u(t),p(t))$. Suppose the exact and numerical state/adjoint pairs lie in a common tube and
$$\max_n\bigl(\|u_n-u(t_n)\|_2+\|p_n-p(t_n)\|_2\bigr)\le C_xh^p.$$
For the state part of this bound, it is sufficient that the hypotheses of [[thm-global-error-from-one-step-defect-and-stability]] hold with a uniform $O(h^{p+1})$ exact-start defect; the coefficient conditions of [[prop-explicit-rk-order-conditions-through-four]] supply that defect for an explicit Runge--Kutta method of order $p\le4$ under that item's $C^4$ and common-tube assumptions. No cited state-error result supplies the adjoint part, which is an independent hypothesis here. Write $b$ and $b_h$ for the column initial/terminal contribution vectors in the continuous and discrete gradient formulas. Assume the discrete running-gradient terms admit vectors $\widehat q_n$ and nonnegative weights $w_n$, $0\le n\le N$, with
$$\nabla J_h=b_h+\sum_{n=0}^N w_n\widehat q_n,\qquad \nabla J=b+\int_0^Tq(t)\,dt,\qquad \sum_{n=0}^Nw_n=T.$$
The weighted discrete representation is an explicit premise; it is not implied by the generic finite state-step adjoint recursion. Suppose
$$\|\widehat q_n-q(t_n,u_n,p_n)\|_2\le C_dh^p,\qquad \|b_h-b\|_2\le C_bh^p,$$
and that the same weights give the quadrature $Q_h(q)=\sum_{n=0}^Nw_nq(t_n)$ satisfying
$$\left\|Q_h(q)-\int_0^Tq(t)\,dt\right\|_2\le C_Qh^p.$$
If $q$ is Lipschitz in $(u,p)$ on the common tube with constant $L_q$ in the sum norm, then
$$\|\nabla J_h-\nabla J\|_2\le\bigl(C_b+T(C_d+L_qC_x)+C_Q\bigr)h^p.$$
The adjoint, derivative-data and quadrature hypotheses are separate from state accuracy; without them the state estimate alone gives no gradient error conclusion.

There is also the following independent method-consistency conclusion. Under the local $C^1$ step-and-cost consistency, derivative stability, derivative Lipschitz, initial-data, terminal-derivative and tube hypotheses of [[lem-local-c1-step-consistency-implies-tangent-adjoint-gradient-order]], the actual numerical graph satisfies
$$\max_n\|D_\theta u_n-D_\theta u(t_n)\|_2\le C_Sh^p,\qquad \max_n\|p_n-p(t_n)\|_2\le C_Ph^p,$$
$$\|\nabla J_h-\nabla J\|_2\le C_Gh^p,$$
with that lemma's explicit constants, together with its state bound. These conclusions derive the global tangent and adjoint errors from local map errors. They do not assume the preceding global state/adjoint bound or weighted representation.

In particular, [[lem-explicit-rk-differentiated-stages-give-local-c1-order]] supplies these local hypotheses for the actual explicit RK state map and the cost using the same tableau, under its common-tube, base $C^2$, and local augmented-order hypotheses. For $p\le4$, its augmented $C^4$ hypothesis and the existing coefficient conditions suffice; jointly $C^5$ base data are an explicit sufficient smoothness condition, and its displayed classical RK4 tableau gives a concrete order-four instance. Generic $p$ is retained through its genuine local augmented-order hypothesis. This branch permits negative or zero RK weights and makes no internal-stage adjoint accuracy claim.

$$D_\theta\Psi_h=D_\theta u+h(b^T\otimes I_d)\bigl(F_YD_\theta Y+F_uD_\theta u+F_\theta\bigr).$$

$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le E_u,\qquad \|p-p_h\|_V\le E_p.$$

$$g[\eta]=D_\theta J(u,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_\theta'[\eta](p)-a_\theta'[\eta](u,p),\qquad g_h[\eta]=D_\theta J_h(u_h,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta](p_h)-a_{\theta,h}'[\eta](u_h,p_h).$$

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $N\ge1$, and for $0\le n\le N$ let $U_n\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_n}$ be open. A finite parameterized state-step graph consists of a $C^1$ initial map $x_0:\Theta\to U_0$ and $C^1$ step maps $\Psi_n:U_n\times\Theta\to U_{n+1}$ for $0\le n<N$, such that the recursion $x_{n+1}(\theta)=\Psi_n(x_n(\theta),\theta)$ is defined for every $\theta$ in the chosen parameter neighborhood. A $C^1$ running objective consists of maps $\ell_n:U_n\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ and a terminal objective $\phi:U_N\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$, all $C^1$. Its reduced objective is
$$J(\theta)=\phi(x_N(\theta),\theta)+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\ell_n(x_n(\theta),\theta).$$
The maps and objective define one finite real-arithmetic graph. A gradient of this graph is the derivative of this finite composition; it is not the derivative of an exact implicit solution unless the step map itself is that solution map.

source_evidence.fullclaim: Let $V$ be a real Hilbert space, let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and write $V^*$ for the continuous real dual. $$\max_n\bigl(\|u_n-u(t_n)\|_2+\|p_n-p(t_n)\|_2\bigr)\le C_xh^p.$$
For the state part of this bound, it is sufficient that the hypotheses of [[thm-global-error-from-one-step-defect-and-stability]] hold with a uniform $O(h^{p+1})$ exact-start defect; the coefficient conditions of [[prop-explicit-rk-order-conditions-through-four]] supply that defect for an explicit Runge--Kutta method of order $p\le4$ under that item's $C^4$ and common-tube assumptions. No cited state-error result supplies the adjoint part, which is an independent hypothesis here. Write $b$ and $b_h$ for the column initial/terminal contribution vectors in the continuous and discrete gradient formulas. Assume the discrete running-gradient terms admit vectors $\widehat q_n$ and nonnegative weights $w_n$, $0\le n\le N$, with
$$\nabla J_h=b_h+\sum_{n=0}^N w_n\widehat q_n,\qquad \nabla J=b+\int_0^Tq(t)\,dt,\qquad \sum_{n=0}^Nw_n=T.$$
The weighted discrete representation is an explicit premise; it is not implied by the generic finite state-step adjoint recursion. Suppose
$$\|\widehat q_n-q(t_n,u_n,p_n)\|_2\le C_dh^p,\qquad \|b_h-b\|_2\le C_bh^p,$$
and that the same weights give the quadrature $Q_h(q)=\sum_{n=0}^Nw_nq(t_n)$ satisfying
$$\left\|Q_h(q)-\int_0^Tq(t)\,dt\right\|_2\le C_Qh^p.$$
If $q$ is Lipschitz in $(u,p)$ on the common tube with constant $L_q$ in the sum norm, then
$$\|\nabla J_h-\nabla J\|_2\le\bigl(C_b+T(C_d+L_qC_x)+C_Q\bigr)h^p.$$
The adjoint, derivative-data and quadrature hypotheses are separate from state accuracy; without them the state estimate alone gives no gradient error conclusion.

There is also the following independent method-consistency conclusion. $$\max_n\|D_\theta u_n-D_\theta u(t_n)\|_2\le C_Sh^p,\qquad \max_n\|p_n-p(t_n)\|_2\le C_Ph^p,$$
$$\|\nabla J_h-\nabla J\|_2\le C_Gh^p,$$
with that lemma's explicit constants, together with its state bound. These conclusions derive the global tangent and adjoint errors from local map errors. They do not assume the preceding global state/adjoint bound or weighted representation.

In particular, [[lem-explicit-rk-differentiated-stages-give-local-c1-order]] supplies these local hypotheses for the actual explicit RK state map and the cost using the same tableau, under its common-tube, base $C^2$, and local augmented-order hypotheses. Let $A_1,\ldots,A_N\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be invertible, with $n,N\ge1$, and let $Q_0$ be orthogonal. For $1\le k\le N$, form the unique positive-diagonal QR factorization
$$A_kQ_{k-1}=Q_kR_k,$$
where $Q_k$ is orthogonal and $R_k$ is upper triangular with positive diagonal $r_{k,ii}$. Put $P_N=A_N\cdots A_1$ and define the exact finite-time log-volume change by $\log|\det P_N|$. Then
$$\log|\det P_N|=\sum_{k=1}^N\sum_{i=1}^n\log r_{k,ii}.$$
No infinite-time Lyapunov exponent or shadowing conclusion follows.

For a numerical log record, define $\sigma_{\min}(A):=\inf_{\|x\|_2=1}\|Ax\|_2$. If $\sigma_{\min}(A_k)\ge\sigma>0$, each exact $r_{k,ii}\ge\sigma$. If positive computed diagonals $\widetilde r_{k,ii}$ satisfy $|\widetilde r_{k,ii}-r_{k,ii}|\le\varepsilon_{k,i}\le\sigma/2$, and each computed logarithm $\widehat l_{k,i}$ satisfies $|\widehat l_{k,i}-\log\widetilde r_{k,ii}|\le\delta_{k,i}$, then
$$\left|\sum_{k,i}\widehat l_{k,i}-\log|\det P_N|\right|\le\sum_{k,i}\left(\frac{2\varepsilon_{k,i}}{\sigma}+\delta_{k,i}\right).$$
If any factor loses rank, this log-volume branch returns failure.

actualproofparagraphs.1.2: Orthogonal factors preserve Euclidean norms, so $\sigma_{\min}(R_k)=\sigma_{\min}(Q_kR_k)=\sigma_{\min}(A_kQ_{k-1})=\sigma_{\min}(A_k)\ge\sigma$. For a fixed $i$, the leading $(i-1)\times(i-1)$ block of $R_k$ is invertible. Choose $x\in\mathbb R^{i-1}$ solving $R_{1:i-1,1:i-1}x=-R_{1:i-1,i}$ and set $z=(x,1,0,\ldots,0)^T$. Upper triangularity gives $R_kz=r_{k,ii}e_i$ and $\|z\|_2\ge1$, so $\sigma_{\min}(R_k)\le\|R_kz\|_2/\|z\|_2\le r_{k,ii}$. For $i=1$, take $z=e_1$. Hence $r_{k,ii}\ge\sigma$. [F1, given, algebra]

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $u_\theta$ solve the parameter-dependent ODE of [[lem-parameter-ode-flow-tangent-on-common-tube]] on $[0,T]$. Let
$$J(\theta)=\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)+\int_0^T\ell(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)\,dt,$$
where $\phi$ and $\ell$ are $C^1$ on a neighborhood of the trajectory tube and their first derivatives are bounded and uniformly continuous there. Let $S=D_\theta u_\theta$ be the tangent from that lemma. Let $p$ solve the terminal adjoint problem
$$-p'(t)=D_u f(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)^Tp(t)+D_u\ell(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)^T,\qquad p(T)=D_u\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)^T.$$
Then
$$\nabla_\theta J=D_\theta\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)^T+D_\theta u_0(\theta)^Tp(0)+\int_0^T\bigl(D_\theta\ell(t,u_\theta,\theta)^T+D_\theta f(t,u_\theta,\theta)^Tp(t)\bigr)\,dt.$$
This formula separates initial, terminal, running-cost and vector-field parameter terms. It applies only while the common-tube and differentiability hypotheses hold.

actualproofparagraphs.1.2: By [F1], the state depends $C^1$ on the parameter and has sensitivity $S$. The chain rule gives the column gradient of the running integrand as $D_\theta\ell(t,u_\theta,\theta)^T+S(t)^TD_u\ell(t,u_\theta,\theta)^T$. The mean-value integral formula, boundedness and uniform continuity of the objective derivatives on the common compact tube, and the uniform first-order state remainder from [F1] make the running first-order remainder $o(\|h\|)$ uniformly in $t$ for a parameter increment $h$. Integration therefore gives its derivative by integrating that column gradient. The terminal chain rule gives $D_\theta\phi^T+S(T)^TD_u\phi^T$. Consequently $\nabla_\theta J=D_\theta\phi^T+S(T)^TD_u\phi^T+\int_0^T(D_\theta\ell^T+S^TD_u\ell^T)\,dt$. [F1, A1, given]
actualproofparagraphs.1.3: In [F2], set $A=D_uf$, $B=D_\theta f$, and $g=D_u\ell^T$. The adjoint equation in the Statement and tangent equation in [F1] satisfy its hypotheses. Transposing that row pairing identity and using $p(T)=D_u\phi^T$ gives $$S(T)^TD_u\phi^T-D_\theta u_0^Tp(0)=\int_0^T(-S^TD_u\ell^T+D_\theta f^Tp)\,dt.$$ [F1, F2, given]
actualproofparagraphs.2.1: Substitute step 1.3 into step 1.2; the terms involving $S^TD_u\ell^T$ cancel, leaving the asserted continuous adjoint gradient formula. [step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra] ∎

$$D_\theta\Psi_h=D_\theta u+h(b^T\otimes I_d)\bigl(F_YD_\theta Y+F_uD_\theta u+F_\theta\bigr).$$

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice and the elliptic state/adjoint setting of [[thm-elliptic-adjoint-reduced-gradient]]. Let $V_h\subseteq V$ be a finite-dimensional conforming space. Let $a_{\theta,h}$ and $\ell_{\theta,h}$ be operator-norm $C^1$ in $\theta$, uniformly coercive on $V_h$, and define the discrete state by $a_{\theta,h}(u_h,v_h)=\ell_{\theta,h}(v_h)$. Let $J_h:V_h\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, and let $p_h\in V_h$ solve $a_{\theta,h}(v_h,p_h)=D_uJ_h(u_h,\theta)[v_h]$. Suppose the parameter derivatives of the discrete forms and loads have specified bounded extensions to $V$ that agree with their values on $V_h$. Let $u,p$ be the exact state and adjoint, and let $u_h,p_h\in V_h$ be their discrete counterparts, with certified energy bounds
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le E_u,\qquad \|p-p_h\|_V\le E_p.$$
For an exact conforming Galerkin solve these bounds may be supplied by [[thm-cea-quasi-optimality-for-conforming-galerkin-approximations]]; for a conforming perturbed solve they may be supplied by [[thm-first-strang-lemma-for-conforming-perturbed-galerkin]], with all load, form, geometry and quadrature defects retained as in [[def-variational-crime-error-framework]]. Define exact and discrete reduced gradients by
$$g[\eta]=D_\theta J(u,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_\theta'[\eta](p)-a_\theta'[\eta](u,p),\qquad g_h[\eta]=D_\theta J_h(u_h,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta](p_h)-a_{\theta,h}'[\eta](u_h,p_h).$$
Assume for $\|\eta\|_2\le1$ that $\|\ell_\theta'[\eta]\|_{V^*}\le M_\ell$, $\|a_\theta'[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le M_a$, the direct-objective defect satisfies $|D_\theta J_h(u_h,\theta)[\eta]-D_\theta J(u,\theta)[\eta]|\le\varepsilon_J$, and the derivative-data defects obey
$$\|\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta]-\ell_\theta'[\eta]\|_{V^*}\le\varepsilon_\ell,\qquad \|a_{\theta,h}'[\eta]-a_\theta'[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le\varepsilon_a.$$
Put $U_*=\max(\|u\|_V,\|u_h\|_V)$ and $P_*=\max(\|p\|_V,\|p_h\|_V)$. Then
$$\|g_h-g\|_{\Theta^*}\le\varepsilon_J+M_\ell E_p+\varepsilon_\ell P_*+M_a(E_uP_*+U_*E_p)+\varepsilon_aU_*P_*.$$
The derivative-data defects are separate obligations: ordinary state and adjoint Strang bounds do not by themselves bound derivative defects.

actualproofparagraphs.1.2: Choose a basis of $V_h$. Coercivity makes the discrete state matrix $K_h(\theta)$ invertible, and its entries and the load coordinates are $C^1$. The identity $K_h(\theta+z)^{-1}-K_h(\theta)^{-1}=-K_h(\theta+z)^{-1}(K_h(\theta+z)-K_h(\theta))K_h(\theta)^{-1}$ shows that its inverse, and hence $u_h(\theta)$, is $C^1$. Differentiating the state equation gives $a_{\theta,h}(w_h,v_h)=\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta](v_h)-a_{\theta,h}'[\eta](u_h,v_h)$. By [F4], $D j_h[\eta]=J_{\theta,h}'[\eta]+D_uJ_h[w_h]$; use the discrete adjoint equation with $v_h=w_h$, then the differentiated state equation with $v_h=p_h$, to obtain the formula for $g_h$ in the Statement. The continuous formula is supplied by [F1]. [F1, F4, given, algebra]

$$\langle w_\eta'(t),v\rangle+a_\theta(t;w_\eta(t),v)=\langle f_\theta'[\eta](t),v\rangle-a_\theta'[\eta](t;u_\theta(t),v),\qquad w_\eta(0)=u_{0,\theta}'[\eta].$$

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice and the differentiable state/adjoint setting of [[thm-parabolic-adjoint-gradient-sensitivity]]. Let $u,p$ and $u_h,p_h$ denote the continuous and semidiscrete state/adjoint pairs, with gradients $g,g_h$ given by that theorem and its finite-dimensional application. Assume $u,p\in H^1(0,T;V)$, the parabolic form and its parameter derivative are uniformly bounded, and the form is coercive with constant $\alpha>0$. Suppose the forward state and time-reversed adjoint both satisfy the hypotheses of [[thm-parabolic-semidiscrete-ritz-error-splitting-and-energy-bound]], with operator-norm $C^1$ comparison maps $P_{u,h}(t),P_{p,h}(t):V\to V_h$. For the state comparison map, set $\rho_u=P_{u,h}u-u$, $\vartheta_u=u_h-P_{u,h}u$, and
$$\mathcal R_u(t)(v_h)=(\rho_u'(t),v_h)_H+a_\theta(t;\rho_u(t),v_h),\qquad \rho_u'=P_{u,h}'(t)u+P_{u,h}(t)u'-u'.$$
In reverse time $s=T-t$, put $q(s)=p(T-s)$ and $\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)=P_{p,h}(T-s)$; define $\rho_p(s)=\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)-q(s)$, $\vartheta_p(s)=p_h(T-s)-\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)$, and $\mathcal R_p(s)(v_h)=(\rho_p'(s),v_h)_H+a_\theta(T-s;v_h,\rho_p(s))$. The projection product rule gives $\rho_p'=\widetilde P_{p,h}'q+\widetilde P_{p,h}q'-q'$, with $\widetilde P_{p,h}'(s)=-P_{p,h}'(T-s)$. The Ritz supplier gives, for $z=u,p$,

Let $\mathcal H=\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$, with square-summability as in [[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]]. Define the diagonal operator $A$ by
$$D(A)=\left\{u\in\mathcal H:\sum_{k\ge1} k^4|u_k|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad (Au)_k=-k^2u_k.$$
Let $g\in\mathcal H$ be the fixed sequence $g_k=1/k$ for odd $k$ and $g_k=0$ for even $k$; membership follows from [[thm-p-series-real-exponents]] with exponent $2$. The split evolution is $u'=Au+g$. For $t\ge0$, define the exact diagonal subflow $E_tu=(e^{-k^2t}u_k)_{k\ge1}$ and the exact translation subflow $B_tu=u+tg$. By [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]] and [[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]], $0<e^{-k^2t}\le1$, so each $E_t$ maps $\mathcal H$ to itself; each $B_t$ does so because $g\in\mathcal H$. The associated Strang modal step is
$$S_h=E_{h/2}\circ B_h\circ E_{h/2},\qquad h>0,$$
where the rightmost map is applied first. Each coordinate of $E_t$ solves $u_k'=-k^2u_k$, and each coordinate of $B_t$ solves $u_k'=g_k$. This is a precisely defined sequence-space model; it records one Dirichlet sine-mode boundary mismatch and makes no general convergence assertion for unbounded PDE operators.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $P_0=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$, $P_1=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$, and
$X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$. In the finite-basis model choose
$S=L=I_2$, $h=0$, $E_{xc}=0$, and the real-linear map
$$G(P)=\bigl(\langle P,P_0\rangle_F-\langle P,P_1\rangle_F\bigr)X+\langle P,X\rangle_F(P_0-P_1).$$
At $P_0$ and $P_1$ the commutator residuals are equal and nonzero, making the
two-vector Gram matrix singular. A solver that reports this singular system
uses the specified baseline fallback, even though the exact capped minimizer
exists.

actualproofparagraphs.2.1: Substitution gives $G(P_0)=X$ and $G(P_1)=-X$. The matrices $X$ and $-X$ have eigenvalues $-1,1$, so both iterates have gap $2$. Direct multiplication gives $[G(P_0),P_0]=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}=[G(P_1),P_1]\ne0.$ [step 1.1, algebra]
actualproofparagraphs.3.1: Writing the common residual as $J$, the Gram matrix is $B_{ij}=\langle J,J\rangle_F=2,\qquad B=\begin{pmatrix}2&2\\2&2\end{pmatrix},$ which is singular. The equality-constrained bordered system has matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2&2&1\\2&2&1\\1&1&0\end{pmatrix}$, whose first two rows coincide, so a solver that reports singularity takes the prescribed fallback. With $C=2$, $c=(1/2,1/2)$ is feasible and minimizes the objective; the objective is constant on $c_1+c_2=1$, so [F2] selects this unique minimum-norm minimizer. If a rank-revealing solver returns it instead of reporting singularity, then $F_{mix}=\tfrac12X-\tfrac12X=0$ has no strict gap, and the proposal algorithm again falls back by its candidate-gap branch. Thus either outcome of this configured solve uses the baseline. [step 2.1, F2, F3, algebra] ∎

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $a,b:U\to\mathbb R^d$ be $C^3$ fields on an open set, and restrict attention to points and time intervals for which the unique local solutions of $x'=a(x)$ and $x'=b(x)$ remain in $U$. Denote their exact solution maps by $\Phi_a^t$ and $\Phi_b^t$. The **Lie split map** applies $a$ and then $b$:
$$L_h:=\Phi_b^h\circ\Phi_a^h.$$
The **Strang split map** applies half of $a$, then $b$, then half of $a$:
$$S_h:=\Phi_a^{h/2}\circ\Phi_b^h\circ\Phi_a^{h/2}.$$
Define the vector-field Lie bracket convention
$$[a,b](y):=Db(y)a(y)-Da(y)b(y).$$
This definition is finite-dimensional. It asserts neither that an unbounded operator has a common invariant domain nor that its commutators are bounded.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $a,b\in C^3(U,\mathbb R^d)$ on an open set and let $K_0\subset K\subset U$, where $K_0$ is compact and $K$ is compact and convex. Assume the exact subflows and their compositions from $K_0$ remain in $K$ for all sufficiently small $h>0$, and the fields and derivatives through order three are bounded on $K$. Uniformly for $y\in K_0$,
$$L_h(y)-\Phi_{a+b}^h(y)=\frac{h^2}{2}[a,b](y)+O(h^3),$$
and the Strang expansion, pointwise in $y$, is
$$S_h(y)-\Phi_{a+b}^h(y)=-\frac{h^3}{24}[a,[a,b]](y)-\frac{h^3}{12}[b,[a,b]](y)+o(h^3).$$
The Strang defect is also uniformly $O(h^3)$ on $K_0$. The maps and bracket use [[def-exact-split-flows-lie-strang-and-bracket]]; the claim is finite-dimensional.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: For a $C^3$ field $c$ and a smooth scalar coordinate function $q(y)=y_j$, define $L_cq:=Dq\,c$. By [F2], differentiating $q(\Phi_c^t(y))$ successively in $t$ gives $L_cq$, $L_c^2q$, and $L_c^3q$, evaluated along the flow. Three uses of [F3] give the expansion through degree two with integral remainder $\frac12\int_0^h(h-s)^2(L_c^3q)(\Phi_c^s(y))\,ds$; [A1] bounds this remainder uniformly by $C h^3$ and continuity at $s=0$ gives cubic coefficient $\frac16L_c^3q(y)$ with pointwise remainder $o(h^3)$. The same reasoning applies successively to the finite flow compositions. [A1, F2, F3, algebra]

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $a,b\in C^3(U,\mathbb R^d)$ define the additive IVP of [[def-additive-ode-and-partition]] and have exact subflows on a common compact convex tube over $[0,T]$. Assume $a,b$ are Lipschitz there with constants $L_a,L_b$, and the exact solution, all split stages, and all numerical states remain in that tube with positive margin. For $h=T/N$ and exact initial data, the exact Lie and Strang split maps of [[def-exact-split-flows-lie-strang-and-bracket]] satisfy
$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\|y_n^{\rm Lie}-y(t_n)\|_2\le C_1h,\qquad \max_{0\le n\le N}\|y_n^{\rm Strang}-y(t_n)\|_2\le C_2h^2.$$
The constants may depend on the tube, the fields, and $T$. For approximate subflows, suppose $\|\widehat\Phi_c^s(u)-\Phi_c^s(u)\|_2\le\epsilon_c(s)$ for $c\in\{a,b\}$ and every admitted starting state $u$. If all approximate compositions stay in the tube, their composed one-step maps are Lipschitz with constant $1+\widehat Lh$, and
$$\epsilon_b(h)+e^{L_bh}\epsilon_a(h)=O(h^2)$$
for Lie and
$$\epsilon_a(h/2)+e^{L_ah/2}\epsilon_b(h)+e^{(L_a/2+L_b)h}\epsilon_a(h/2)=O(h^3)$$
for Strang, then the same respective global orders hold. These additional conditions keep subflow-solver errors separate from splitting errors.

actualproofparagraphs.2.1: Fix $h_0>0$ within the admitted step range. source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $P\in\mathcal P_r$ and let $F=F(P)$ be Hermitian. Define the level-shifted
matrix $F_s=F+s(I-P)$ for real $s$, and define the Hermitian compressions
$$F_{occ}:=(PFP)|_{\operatorname{ran}P},\qquad F_{vir}:=((I-P)F(I-P))|_{\operatorname{ran}(I-P)}.$$
For either finite-dimensional Hermitian block, $\sigma$ denotes its finite
eigenvalue set. When $PF=FP$, these compressions are the restrictions of $F$
to the two invariant subspaces. Then
$$\Pi_r(F_s)=P$$
if and only if $PF=FP$ and
$$\max\sigma(F_{occ})<\min\sigma(F_{vir})+s.$$
The strict inequality is the shifted occupied/unoccupied ordering. A level shift
can change the map when either commutation or this ordering fails.

actualproofparagraphs.3.1: Conversely, if $\Pi_r(F_s)=P$, the isolated lowest-$r$ spectral projector commutes with $F_s$ by [F2]. Since $[s(I-P),P]=0$, this gives $[F,P]=0$, so the two restrictions in the statement are defined. The map's strict-gap domain in [F2] and uniqueness in [L1] require the largest occupied eigenvalue to be strictly smaller than the smallest shifted virtual eigenvalue; equality closes the $r$th gap, while reverse ordering selects a different spectral block. Hence the displayed ordering holds. [given, step 1.1, F1, F2, L1] ∎

Assume Countable Choice and the setting of [[def-parameterized-elliptic-variational-problem]]. On an open neighborhood $\Theta_0\subseteq\Theta$, suppose the same constants $M<\infty$ and $\alpha>0$ give boundedness and coercivity for every $a_\theta$, and $\theta\mapsto A_\theta$ and $\theta\mapsto\ell_\theta$ are operator-norm $C^1$. Then each state $u_\theta$ exists uniquely, the map $\theta\mapsto u_\theta\in V$ is $C^1$, and for each direction $\eta\in\mathbb R^m$ its derivative $w_\eta=D_\theta u_\theta[\eta]$ is the unique solution of
$$a_\theta(w_\eta,v)=D_\theta\ell_\theta[\eta](v)-D_\theta a_\theta[\eta](u_\theta,v)\qquad(v\in V).$$
Uniform coercivity is required on the parameter neighborhood; no differentiability conclusion is asserted at a loss of coercivity.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: For each $\theta\in\Theta_0$, apply [F1] to $a_\theta$ and $\ell_\theta$; this gives a unique $u_\theta$ and the bound $\|u_\theta\|_V\le\alpha^{-1}\|\ell_\theta\|_{V^*}$. actualproofparagraphs.2.2: For each direction $h\in\mathbb R^m$, define $w_h$ by $a_\theta(w_h,v)=D\ell_\theta[h](v)-\bigl(DA_\theta[h]u_\theta\bigr)(v)$. Assume Countable Choice and the elliptic state/adjoint setting of [[thm-elliptic-adjoint-reduced-gradient]]. Let $V_h\subseteq V$ be a finite-dimensional conforming space. Let $a_{\theta,h}$ and $\ell_{\theta,h}$ be operator-norm $C^1$ in $\theta$, uniformly coercive on $V_h$, and define the discrete state by $a_{\theta,h}(u_h,v_h)=\ell_{\theta,h}(v_h)$. Let $J_h:V_h\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, and let $p_h\in V_h$ solve $a_{\theta,h}(v_h,p_h)=D_uJ_h(u_h,\theta)[v_h]$. Suppose the parameter derivatives of the discrete forms and loads have specified bounded extensions to $V$ that agree with their values on $V_h$. Let $u,p$ be the exact state and adjoint, and let $u_h,p_h\in V_h$ be their discrete counterparts, with certified energy bounds
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le E_u,\qquad \|p-p_h\|_V\le E_p.$$
For an exact conforming Galerkin solve these bounds may be supplied by [[thm-cea-quasi-optimality-for-conforming-galerkin-approximations]]; for a conforming perturbed solve they may be supplied by [[thm-first-strang-lemma-for-conforming-perturbed-galerkin]], with all load, form, geometry and quadrature defects retained as in [[def-variational-crime-error-framework]]. Define exact and discrete reduced gradients by
$$g[\eta]=D_\theta J(u,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_\theta'[\eta](p)-a_\theta'[\eta](u,p),\qquad g_h[\eta]=D_\theta J_h(u_h,\theta)[\eta]+\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta](p_h)-a_{\theta,h}'[\eta](u_h,p_h).$$
Assume for $\|\eta\|_2\le1$ that $\|\ell_\theta'[\eta]\|_{V^*}\le M_\ell$, $\|a_\theta'[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le M_a$, the direct-objective defect satisfies $|D_\theta J_h(u_h,\theta)[\eta]-D_\theta J(u,\theta)[\eta]|\le\varepsilon_J$, and the derivative-data defects obey
$$\|\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta]-\ell_\theta'[\eta]\|_{V^*}\le\varepsilon_\ell,\qquad \|a_{\theta,h}'[\eta]-a_\theta'[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le\varepsilon_a.$$
Put $U_*=\max(\|u\|_V,\|u_h\|_V)$ and $P_*=\max(\|p\|_V,\|p_h\|_V)$. Then
$$\|g_h-g\|_{\Theta^*}\le\varepsilon_J+M_\ell E_p+\varepsilon_\ell P_*+M_a(E_uP_*+U_*E_p)+\varepsilon_aU_*P_*.$$
The derivative-data defects are separate obligations: ordinary state and adjoint Strang bounds do not by themselves bound derivative defects.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: Apply [F2] to an exact conforming Galerkin state and its adjoint, or [F3] to each conforming perturbed equation, using the transposed form $a^\dagger(v,w)=a(w,v)$ for the adjoint. Transposition preserves boundedness and coercivity constants. Under [A1], the resulting two bounds are $E_u,E_p$, with all applicable form and load defects, including geometry and quadrature contributions, retained as specified by [F3]. [A1, F2, F3]
actualproofparagraphs.1.2: Choose a basis of $V_h$. Coercivity makes the discrete state matrix $K_h(\theta)$ invertible, and its entries and the load coordinates are $C^1$. The identity $K_h(\theta+z)^{-1}-K_h(\theta)^{-1}=-K_h(\theta+z)^{-1}(K_h(\theta+z)-K_h(\theta))K_h(\theta)^{-1}$ shows that its inverse, and hence $u_h(\theta)$, is $C^1$. Differentiating the state equation gives $a_{\theta,h}(w_h,v_h)=\ell_{\theta,h}'[\eta](v_h)-a_{\theta,h}'[\eta](u_h,v_h)$. By [F4], $D j_h[\eta]=J_{\theta,h}'[\eta]+D_uJ_h[w_h]$; use the discrete adjoint equation with $v_h=w_h$, then the differentiated state equation with $v_h=p_h$, to obtain the formula for $g_h$ in the Statement. The continuous formula is supplied by [F1]. [F1, F4, given, algebra]
