source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice, and use the real evolution triple $(V,H,V^*)$ of [[def-parameterized-parabolic-variational-problem]]. On an open parameter set $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, assume the state map $\theta\mapsto u_\theta$ is Fr\'echet differentiable into $W(0,T;V)$, with derivative $w_\eta$ in direction $\eta\in\mathbb R^m$. Assume, for every $v\in V$ and almost every $t$,
$$\langle w_\eta'(t),v\rangle+a_\theta(t;w_\eta(t),v)=\langle f_\theta'[\eta](t),v\rangle-a_\theta'[\eta](t;u_\theta(t),v),\qquad w_\eta(0)=u_{0,\theta}'[\eta].$$
Let $\phi:H\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$, and let $L:[0,T]\times V\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be measurable in time and $C^1$ in $(u,\theta)$ for almost every time, with a common integrable majorant that justifies differentiating its time integral. Assume $D_u\phi$ is represented by an element of $H$ and $D_uL(t,u_\theta,\theta)\in V^*$ is square-integrable in time. Suppose the adjoint $p\in W(0,T;V)$ satisfies
$$-\langle p'(t),v\rangle+a_\theta(t;v,p(t))=D_uL(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)[v],\qquad p(T)=\nabla_H\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta).$$
Then for $j(\theta)=\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)+\int_0^T L(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)\,dt$,
$$D j(\theta)[\eta]=D_\theta\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)[\eta]+(p(0),u_{0,\theta}'[\eta])_H+\int_0^T\left(D_\theta L(t,u_\theta,\theta)[\eta]+\langle f_\theta'[\eta](t),p(t)\rangle-a_\theta'[\eta](t;u_\theta(t),p(t))\right)dt.$$
This is conditional on the displayed differentiable state and adjoint; it does not prove either exists. The adjoint form is transposed as shown, so symmetry of $a_\theta$ is not required.

actualproofparagraphs.1.2: Apply [F2] to $w_\eta$ and $p$. By the adjoint equation with $v=w_\eta$ and the linearized state equation with $v=p$, the integrand in its right side is $$\langle p',w_\eta\rangle+\langle w_\eta',p\rangle=a_\theta(t;w_\eta,p)-D_uL[w_\eta]+\langle f_\theta'[\eta],p\rangle-a_\theta(t;w_\eta,p)-a_\theta'[\eta](u_\theta,p),$$ so the two terms containing $a_\theta(t;w_\eta,p)$ cancel. Countable Choice enters here through the pairing result [F2]. [A1, F2, given, algebra]

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice and the differentiable state/adjoint setting of [[thm-parabolic-adjoint-gradient-sensitivity]]. Let $u,p$ and $u_h,p_h$ denote the continuous and semidiscrete state/adjoint pairs, with gradients $g,g_h$ given by that theorem and its finite-dimensional application. Assume $u,p\in H^1(0,T;V)$, the parabolic form and its parameter derivative are uniformly bounded, and the form is coercive with constant $\alpha>0$. Suppose the forward state and time-reversed adjoint both satisfy the hypotheses of [[thm-parabolic-semidiscrete-ritz-error-splitting-and-energy-bound]], with operator-norm $C^1$ comparison maps $P_{u,h}(t),P_{p,h}(t):V\to V_h$. For the state comparison map, set $\rho_u=P_{u,h}u-u$, $\vartheta_u=u_h-P_{u,h}u$, and
$$\mathcal R_u(t)(v_h)=(\rho_u'(t),v_h)_H+a_\theta(t;\rho_u(t),v_h),\qquad \rho_u'=P_{u,h}'(t)u+P_{u,h}(t)u'-u'.$$
In reverse time $s=T-t$, put $q(s)=p(T-s)$ and $\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)=P_{p,h}(T-s)$; define $\rho_p(s)=\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)-q(s)$, $\vartheta_p(s)=p_h(T-s)-\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)$, and $\mathcal R_p(s)(v_h)=(\rho_p'(s),v_h)_H+a_\theta(T-s;v_h,\rho_p(s))$. The projection product rule gives $\rho_p'=\widetilde P_{p,h}'q+\widetilde P_{p,h}q'-q'$, with $\widetilde P_{p,h}'(s)=-P_{p,h}'(T-s)$. The Ritz supplier gives, for $z=u,p$,
$$\|z-z_h\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}\le E_z:=\|\rho_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}+\alpha^{-1/2}\left(\|\vartheta_z(0)\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|\mathcal R_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2\right)^{1/2},$$
where the adjoint's initial trace means its terminal trace in original time. In particular, $\mathcal R_z$ contains the derivative of the time-dependent projection; it cannot be dropped from this hypothesis.

For $\|\eta\|_2\le1$, assume $\|D_\theta f[\eta]\|_{L^2(V^*)}\le M_f$, $\|D_\theta a(t)[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le M_a$ a.e., and define $U_*:=\max(\|u\|_{L^2(V)},\|u_h\|_{L^2(V)})$, $P_*:=\max(\|p\|_{L^2(V)},\|p_h\|_{L^2(V)})$, $P_{0,*}:=\max(\|p(0)\|_H,\|p_h(0)\|_H)$, and $U_0':=\|D_\theta u_0\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,H)}$. Suppose the discrete direct-objective derivative differs from the continuous direct-objective derivative $D_\theta\phi+\int_0^T D_\theta L\,dt$ by at most $\varepsilon_J$ in $\Theta^*$; suppose also $\|D_\theta u_{0,h}-D_\theta u_0\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,H)}\le\varepsilon_0$, $\|D_\theta f_h-D_\theta f\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,L^2(V^*))}\le\varepsilon_f$, and $\|D_\theta a_h-D_\theta a\|_{L^\infty(0,T;\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,\mathcal L(V,V^*)))}\le\varepsilon_a$. Put $E_{p,0}=\|p_h(0)-p(0)\|_H$. Then
$$\|g_h-g\|_{(\mathbb R^m)^*}\le \varepsilon_J+U_0'E_{p,0}+P_{0,*}\varepsilon_0+M_fE_p+\varepsilon_fP_*+M_a(E_uP_*+U_*E_p)+\varepsilon_aU_*P_*.$$
The derivative-data and trace defects are additional assumptions; an energy estimate for the state alone does not imply this gradient bound.

The comparison $\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)=P_{p,h}(T-s)$ is operator-norm $C^1$ and $\widetilde P_{p,h}'(s)=-P_{p,h}'(T-s)$. Let $p\ge1$ be an integer, $T>0$, $h=T/N\le h_0\le1$, and $t_n=nh$. The state dimension $d$ and parameter dimension $m$ are fixed. All vector norms are Euclidean and all matrix norms are their induced operator norms; gradients are columns.

Consider the continuous objective
$$J(\theta)=\phi(u(T,\theta),\theta)+\int_0^T\ell(t,u(t,\theta),\theta)\,dt,$$
and the actual finite graph
$$x_{n+1}=\Psi_n(x_n,\theta),\qquad J_h(\theta)=\phi_h(x_N,\theta)+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}L_n(x_n,\theta).$$
Assume the hypotheses of the continuous flow-tangent and adjoint-gradient results hold on a common tube. Write $\Phi_n(x,\theta)$ for the exact flow from $t_n$ to $t_{n+1}$ and
$$K_n(x,\theta)=\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}}\ell(t,u(t;t_n,x,\theta),\theta)\,dt.$$
These exact maps and the actual numerical maps are $C^1$ on open neighborhoods of the admitted state and parameter sets. For every relevant $n$, all states $x_n,u(t_n)$ and the segment joining them belong to a convex admitted state set. All estimates below hold uniformly on those sets and a fixed parameter neighborhood, independently of $N,n$.

For $r=e,h$, define
$$A_n^e=D_x\Phi_n,\quad B_n^e=D_\theta\Phi_n,\quad c_n^e=D_xK_n^T,\quad d_n^e=D_\theta K_n^T,$$
$$A_n^h=D_x\Psi_n,\quad B_n^h=D_\theta\Psi_n,\quad c_n^h=D_xL_n^T,\quad d_n^h=D_\theta L_n^T.$$
Suppose constants $c_v,c_1,L,M,H\ge0$ satisfy, at each admitted $(x,\theta)$,
$$\|\Psi_n-\Phi_n\|\le c_vh^{p+1},$$
$$\|A_n^h-A_n^e\|,\ \|B_n^h-B_n^e\|,\ \|c_n^h-c_n^e\|,\ \|d_n^h-d_n^e\|\le c_1h^{p+1},$$
$$\|A_n^r\|\le1+Lh,\qquad \|B_n^r\|,\ \|c_n^r\|,\ \|d_n^r\|\le Mh.$$
Each of $A_n^e,B_n^e,c_n^e,d_n^e$ is Lipschitz in $x$, with constant at most $Hh$.

Let $S_0=D_\theta u(0,\theta)$ and $S_0^h=D_\theta x_0(\theta)$. Assume
$$\|x_0-u(0)\|\le c_0h^p,\qquad \|S_0^h-S_0\|\le c_{s0}h^p,\qquad \|S_0\|\le M_0.$$
The terminal costs are $C^1$. The exact columns $D_x\phi^T,D_\theta\phi^T$ have norm at most $M_\phi$ and are Lipschitz in $x$ with constant $H_\phi$; at the same admitted $(x,\theta)$,
$$\|D_x\phi_h^T-D_x\phi^T\|,\ \|D_\theta\phi_h^T-D_\theta\phi^T\|\le C_\phi h^p.$$
No terminal value-error hypothesis is needed for the gradient conclusion.

Let $S_n^h=D_\theta x_n$, and let $p_n^h$ be the exact discrete adjoint of this numerical graph. Let $S(t)=D_\theta u(t)$ and let $p(t)$ be the continuous adjoint with terminal value $D_x\phi(u(T),\theta)^T$. Define
$$E=e^{LT},\quad X=E(c_0+Tc_v),\quad \overline S=E(M_0+TM),\quad \overline P=E(M_\phi+TM),$$
$$R=c_1+HX,\quad C_S=E\{c_{s0}+TR(\overline S+1)\},\quad D=C_\phi+H_\phi X,$$
$$C_P=E\{D+TR(\overline P+1)\},$$
$$C_G=D+c_{s0}\overline P+(M_0+c_{s0})C_P+T\{R(1+\overline P)+MC_P\}.$$
Then
$$\max_n\|x_n-u(t_n)\|\le Xh^p,\qquad \max_n\|S_n^h-S(t_n)\|\le C_Sh^p,$$
$$\max_n\|p_n^h-p(t_n)\|\le C_Ph^p,\qquad \|\nabla J_h-\nabla J\|\le C_Gh^p.$$
These conclusions assume local value and first-derivative consistency, rather than a global adjoint-error estimate. They require no representation by nonnegative quadrature weights.

$$x_{n+1}=\Psi_n(x_n,\theta),\qquad J_h(\theta)=\phi_h(x_N,\theta)+\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}L_n(x_n,\theta).$$
Assume the hypotheses of the continuous flow-tangent and adjoint-gradient results hold on a common tube. Write $\Phi_n(x,\theta)$ for the exact flow from $t_n$ to $t_{n+1}$ and
$$K_n(x,\theta)=\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}}\ell(t,u(t;t_n,x,\theta),\theta)\,dt.$$
These exact maps and the actual numerical maps are $C^1$ on open neighborhoods of the admitted state and parameter sets. For every relevant $n$, all states $x_n,u(t_n)$ and the segment joining them belong to a convex admitted state set. All estimates below hold uniformly on those sets and a fixed parameter neighborhood, independently of $N,n$.

For $r=e,h$, define
$$A_n^e=D_x\Phi_n,\quad B_n^e=D_\theta\Phi_n,\quad c_n^e=D_xK_n^T,\quad d_n^e=D_\theta K_n^T,$$

$$\|\Psi_n-\Phi_n\|\le c_vh^{p+1},$$
$$\|A_n^h-A_n^e\|,\ \|B_n^h-B_n^e\|,\ \|c_n^h-c_n^e\|,\ \|d_n^h-d_n^e\|\le c_1h^{p+1},$$
$$\|A_n^r\|\le1+Lh,\qquad \|B_n^r\|,\ \|c_n^r\|,\ \|d_n^r\|\le Mh.$$
Each of $A_n^e,B_n^e,c_n^e,d_n^e$ is Lipschitz in $x$, with constant at most $Hh$.

Let $S_0=D_\theta u(0,\theta)$ and $S_0^h=D_\theta x_0(\theta)$. Assume
$$\|x_0-u(0)\|\le c_0h^p,\qquad \|S_0^h-S_0\|\le c_{s0}h^p,\qquad \|S_0\|\le M_0.$$
The terminal costs are $C^1$. The exact columns $D_x\phi^T,D_\theta\phi^T$ have norm at most $M_\phi$ and are Lipschitz in $x$ with constant $H_\phi$; at the same admitted $(x,\theta)$,
$$\|D_x\phi_h^T-D_x\phi^T\|,\ \|D_\theta\phi_h^T-D_\theta\phi^T\|\le C_\phi h^p.$$
No terminal value-error hypothesis is needed for the gradient conclusion.

Let $S_n^h=D_\theta x_n$, and let $p_n^h$ be the exact discrete adjoint of this numerical graph. Let $S(t)=D_\theta u(t)$ and let $p(t)$ be the continuous adjoint with terminal value $D_x\phi(u(T),\theta)^T$. Define
$$E=e^{LT},\quad X=E(c_0+Tc_v),\quad \overline S=E(M_0+TM),\quad \overline P=E(M_\phi+TM),$$
$$R=c_1+HX,\quad C_S=E\{c_{s0}+TR(\overline S+1)\},\quad D=C_\phi+H_\phi X,$$
$$C_P=E\{D+TR(\overline P+1)\},$$
$$C_G=D+c_{s0}\overline P+(M_0+c_{s0})C_P+T\{R(1+\overline P)+MC_P\}.$$

$$\max_n\|x_n-u(t_n)\|\le Xh^p,\qquad \max_n\|S_n^h-S(t_n)\|\le C_Sh^p,$$
$$\max_n\|p_n^h-p(t_n)\|\le C_Ph^p,\qquad \|\nabla J_h-\nabla J\|\le C_Gh^p.$$
These conclusions assume local value and first-derivative consistency, rather than a global adjoint-error estimate. They require no representation by nonnegative quadrature weights.

$$Y_i=x+h\sum_{j<i}a_{ij}f(t_n+c_jh,Y_j,\theta),$$
$$\Psi_n=x+h\sum_i b_if(t_n+c_ih,Y_i,\theta),\qquad L_n=h\sum_i b_i\ell(t_n+c_ih,Y_i,\theta).$$
These are exact finite-stage maps, not outputs of a stopped implicit solver.

Assume $f:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^d$ and $\ell:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ are $C^2$ on an open convex time-state-parameter domain. On a common compact convex subset with positive margin in $\mathcal D$, their derivatives through order two are uniformly bounded. All admitted local exact trajectories, all numerical trajectories and stages, and all needed joining segments lie in this domain and common tube, uniformly over the fixed parameter neighborhood and $h\le h_0$. Stage times outside $[t_n,t_{n+1}]$ are included when the tableau has such abscissae. Unique admitted local flows are assumed as in the flow-tangent supplier.

Put $r=d+m$, $E=[I_d\ 0]\in\mathbb R^{d\times r}$ and $E_\theta=[0\ I_m]\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}$. Consider the autonomous augmented system, with components $t,u,\vartheta,C,V,g$,
$$t'=1,\quad \vartheta'=0,\quad u'=f(t,u,\vartheta),\quad C'=\ell(t,u,\vartheta),$$
$$V'=f_u(t,u,\vartheta)V+f_\theta(t,u,\vartheta)E_\theta,$$
$$g'=V^T\ell_u(t,u,\vartheta)^T+E_\theta^T\ell_\theta(t,u,\vartheta)^T.$$
For every admitted local start use $(t_n,x,\theta,0,E,0)$. Suppose application of the same tableau to this augmented system has uniform exact-start defect at most $C_a h^{p+1}$, for an integer $p\ge1$, on a common compact convex augmented tube with positive margin. Then the actual maps $\Psi_n,L_n$ satisfy all local value, first-derivative, $1+Lh$ derivative-stability, $Mh$ derivative-size, and $Hh$ exact-derivative Lipschitz hypotheses of [[lem-local-c1-step-consistency-implies-tangent-adjoint-gradient-order]], with constants independent of $n,N$. Subject to that lemma's initial and terminal hypotheses, their actual differentiated graph tangents, exact reverse adjoints, and reduced gradients consequently have order-$p$ global error.

A concrete sufficient instantiation for $1\le p\le4$ is that this augmented vector field is $C^4$ with bounded derivatives through order four on its admitted compact convex tube and the tableau satisfies the coefficient equations through order $p$ in [[prop-explicit-rk-order-conditions-through-four]]. Jointly $C^5$ base data $f,\ell$ with bounded derivatives through order five on the base tube are sufficient for this augmented $C^4$ condition. The classical RK4 tableau
$$a_{21}=a_{32}=\tfrac12,\quad a_{43}=1,\quad b=(\tfrac16,\tfrac13,\tfrac13,\tfrac16),\quad c=(0,\tfrac12,\tfrac12,1),$$
with all other $a_{ij}=0$, therefore gives the claimed order-four tangent, nodal-adjoint and gradient approximation under these hypotheses. For general $p$, retain the explicit local augmented-defect hypothesis above; no higher-order coefficient theorem is being asserted.

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ and $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d\times\Theta$ be open, and let $f:D\to\mathbb R^d$ be continuously differentiable. Let $V_\theta\subseteq\Theta$ be open and $u_0:V_\theta\to\mathbb R^d$ be $C^1$. Assume there is a bounded convex open set $O\subset D$ with compact closure in $D$ such that for every $\theta\in V_\theta$ the unique solution of $u'=f(t,u,\theta)$, $u(0)=u_0(\theta)$, exists on $[0,T]$, and all triples $(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)$ lie in $O$. Then $\theta\mapsto u_\theta$ is $C^1$ as a map to $C([0,T];\mathbb R^d)$. For any $\theta_0\in V_\theta$, its tangent matrix $S(t)=D_\theta u_\theta(t)|_{\theta=\theta_0}$ is the unique solution of
$$S'(t)=D_u f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0)S(t)+D_\theta f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0),\qquad S(0)=D u_0(\theta_0).$$
The result is local to the stated common compact tube and claims no differentiability outside it.

actualproofparagraphs.1.2: Put $A(t)=D_u f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0)$ and let $B_j(t)$ be column $j$ of $D_\theta f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0)$. For each parameter coordinate $j$, the augmented vector $Z_j=(S_{\cdot j},1)$ solves the homogeneous linear system $$Z_j'(t)=\begin{pmatrix}A(t)&B_j(t)\\0&0\end{pmatrix}Z_j(t),\qquad Z_j(0)=\begin{pmatrix}D u_0(\theta_0)_{\cdot j}\\1\end{pmatrix}.$$ Embed $Z_j(0)$ as one column of a square $(d+1)\times(d+1)$ initial matrix, with all other columns zero. The unique linear matrix solution supplied by [F5] has that vector solution as the selected column. Thus the tangent equation has a unique solution for each of the finitely many columns. [A1, F5, construct]
actualproofparagraphs.3.1: Let $E_h(t)=\delta_h(t)-S(t)h$, and let $r_0(h)=u_0(\theta_0+h)-u_0(\theta_0)-D u_0(\theta_0)h$. The Volterra equations and the field remainder $\rho_h$ from step 2.1 give $E_h(t)=r_0(h)+\int_0^t\bigl(A(s)E_h(s)+\rho_h(s)\bigr)ds$, where $A(s)=D_u f(s,u_{\theta_0}(s),\theta_0)$. By [F4], $\|E_h(t)\|_2\le\|r_0(h)\|_2+T\sup_s\|\rho_h(s)\|_2+L\int_0^t\|E_h(s)\|_2ds$. Both first terms are $o(\|h\|_2)$ by step 2.1 and differentiability of $u_0$. Applying [F3] yields $\sup_t\|E_h(t)\|_2=o(\|h\|_2)$. Thus the Fréchet derivative at $\theta_0$ exists and equals $S$. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.2, step 2.1]

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $u_\theta$ solve the parameter-dependent ODE of [[lem-parameter-ode-flow-tangent-on-common-tube]] on $[0,T]$. Let
$$J(\theta)=\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)+\int_0^T\ell(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)\,dt,$$
where $\phi$ and $\ell$ are $C^1$ on a neighborhood of the trajectory tube and their first derivatives are bounded and uniformly continuous there. Let $S=D_\theta u_\theta$ be the tangent from that lemma. Let $p$ solve the terminal adjoint problem
$$-p'(t)=D_u f(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)^Tp(t)+D_u\ell(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)^T,\qquad p(T)=D_u\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)^T.$$
Then
$$\nabla_\theta J=D_\theta\phi(u_\theta(T),\theta)^T+D_\theta u_0(\theta)^Tp(0)+\int_0^T\bigl(D_\theta\ell(t,u_\theta,\theta)^T+D_\theta f(t,u_\theta,\theta)^Tp(t)\bigr)\,dt.$$
This formula separates initial, terminal, running-cost and vector-field parameter terms. It applies only while the common-tube and differentiability hypotheses hold.

actualproofparagraphs.1.3: In [F2], set $A=D_uf$, $B=D_\theta f$, and $g=D_u\ell^T$. The adjoint equation in the Statement and tangent equation in [F1] satisfy its hypotheses. Transposing that row pairing identity and using $p(T)=D_u\phi^T$ gives $$S(T)^TD_u\phi^T-D_\theta u_0^Tp(0)=\int_0^T(-S^TD_u\ell^T+D_\theta f^Tp)\,dt.$$ [F1, F2, given]
actualproofparagraphs.2.1: Substitute step 1.3 into step 1.2; the terms involving $S^TD_u\ell^T$ cancel, leaving the asserted continuous adjoint gradient formula. [step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra] ∎

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume Countable Choice and the differentiable state/adjoint setting of [[thm-parabolic-adjoint-gradient-sensitivity]]. Let $u,p$ and $u_h,p_h$ denote the continuous and semidiscrete state/adjoint pairs, with gradients $g,g_h$ given by that theorem and its finite-dimensional application. Assume $u,p\in H^1(0,T;V)$, the parabolic form and its parameter derivative are uniformly bounded, and the form is coercive with constant $\alpha>0$. Suppose the forward state and time-reversed adjoint both satisfy the hypotheses of [[thm-parabolic-semidiscrete-ritz-error-splitting-and-energy-bound]], with operator-norm $C^1$ comparison maps $P_{u,h}(t),P_{p,h}(t):V\to V_h$. For the state comparison map, set $\rho_u=P_{u,h}u-u$, $\vartheta_u=u_h-P_{u,h}u$, and
$$\mathcal R_u(t)(v_h)=(\rho_u'(t),v_h)_H+a_\theta(t;\rho_u(t),v_h),\qquad \rho_u'=P_{u,h}'(t)u+P_{u,h}(t)u'-u'.$$
In reverse time $s=T-t$, put $q(s)=p(T-s)$ and $\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)=P_{p,h}(T-s)$; define $\rho_p(s)=\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)-q(s)$, $\vartheta_p(s)=p_h(T-s)-\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)q(s)$, and $\mathcal R_p(s)(v_h)=(\rho_p'(s),v_h)_H+a_\theta(T-s;v_h,\rho_p(s))$. The projection product rule gives $\rho_p'=\widetilde P_{p,h}'q+\widetilde P_{p,h}q'-q'$, with $\widetilde P_{p,h}'(s)=-P_{p,h}'(T-s)$. The Ritz supplier gives, for $z=u,p$,
$$\|z-z_h\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}\le E_z:=\|\rho_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}+\alpha^{-1/2}\left(\|\vartheta_z(0)\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|\mathcal R_z\|_{L^2(0,T;V_h^*)}^2\right)^{1/2},$$
where the adjoint's initial trace means its terminal trace in original time. In particular, $\mathcal R_z$ contains the derivative of the time-dependent projection; it cannot be dropped from this hypothesis.

For $\|\eta\|_2\le1$, assume $\|D_\theta f[\eta]\|_{L^2(V^*)}\le M_f$, $\|D_\theta a(t)[\eta]\|_{\mathcal L(V,V^*)}\le M_a$ a.e., and define $U_*:=\max(\|u\|_{L^2(V)},\|u_h\|_{L^2(V)})$, $P_*:=\max(\|p\|_{L^2(V)},\|p_h\|_{L^2(V)})$, $P_{0,*}:=\max(\|p(0)\|_H,\|p_h(0)\|_H)$, and $U_0':=\|D_\theta u_0\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,H)}$. Suppose the discrete direct-objective derivative differs from the continuous direct-objective derivative $D_\theta\phi+\int_0^T D_\theta L\,dt$ by at most $\varepsilon_J$ in $\Theta^*$; suppose also $\|D_\theta u_{0,h}-D_\theta u_0\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,H)}\le\varepsilon_0$, $\|D_\theta f_h-D_\theta f\|_{\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,L^2(V^*))}\le\varepsilon_f$, and $\|D_\theta a_h-D_\theta a\|_{L^\infty(0,T;\mathcal L(\mathbb R^m,\mathcal L(V,V^*)))}\le\varepsilon_a$. Put $E_{p,0}=\|p_h(0)-p(0)\|_H$. Then
$$\|g_h-g\|_{(\mathbb R^m)^*}\le \varepsilon_J+U_0'E_{p,0}+P_{0,*}\varepsilon_0+M_fE_p+\varepsilon_fP_*+M_a(E_uP_*+U_*E_p)+\varepsilon_aU_*P_*.$$
The derivative-data and trace defects are additional assumptions; an energy estimate for the state alone does not imply this gradient bound.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: For the forward state, the product rule [F3] gives $\rho_u'=P_{u,h}'u+P_{u,h}u'-u'$, so the residual in [F2] is exactly the one displayed in the Statement. Apply the energy estimate in [F2] to $\vartheta_u$; it gives $\|\vartheta_u\|_{L^2(V)}\le\alpha^{-1/2}(\|\vartheta_u(0)\|_H^2+\alpha^{-1}\|\mathcal R_u\|_{L^2(V_h^*)}^2)^{1/2}$. Since $u-u_h=-\rho_u-\vartheta_u$, the triangle inequality proves the stated $E_u$ bound. [A1, F2, F3, given, algebra]
actualproofparagraphs.2.1: Set $s=T-t$ and $q(s)=p(T-s)$. The backward adjoint equation becomes a forward parabolic variational equation with transposed form $a_\theta(T-s;v,w)$, which has the same boundedness and coercivity constants. The comparison $\widetilde P_{p,h}(s)=P_{p,h}(T-s)$ is operator-norm $C^1$ and $\widetilde P_{p,h}'(s)=-P_{p,h}'(T-s)$. By [F3], its residual contains $\widetilde P_{p,h}'q+\widetilde P_{p,h}q'-q'$; apply the energy estimate in [F2] and the splitting $p-p_h=-\rho_p-\vartheta_p$ to get the stated $E_p$ bound by the same triangle inequality as step 1.1. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1, construct]
actualproofparagraphs.3.1: Subtract the two gradient formulas [F1]. The direct term contributes $\varepsilon_J$. For the initial pairing, add and subtract $(p_h(0),D_\theta u_0)$; Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the difference by $U_0'E_{p,0}+P_{0,*}\varepsilon_0$. In the forcing term, add and subtract $D_\theta f[p_h]$; the derivative-data defect is at most $\varepsilon_fP_*$, and the exact derivative contributes at most $M_fE_p$ by step 2.1. Thus the direct, initial, and forcing contributions are bounded by the first four terms in the stated gradient estimate. [A1, F1, step 2.1, given, algebra]

For $n\ge2$ and $1\le r<n$, the set $\mathcal D_r$ of
[[def-admissible-hermitian-density-domain]] is nonempty, closed, and convex in
$\mathbb H_n$, and complete in the Frobenius metric.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: The diagonal matrix $D_0=\operatorname{diag}(1,\ldots,1,0,\ldots,0)$ with $r$ ones is Hermitian, satisfies $0\preceq D_0\preceq I_n$, and has trace $r$. Thus $D_0\in\mathcal D_r$, so the domain is nonempty. [given, F1, construct]
actualproofparagraphs.2.1: For every fixed $x\in\mathbb C^n$, entrywise convergence gives $x^*D_kx\to x^*Dx$ and $x^*(I_n-D_k)x\to x^*(I_n-D)x$. Since both sequences are nonnegative, their limits are nonnegative, so $0\preceq D\preceq I_n$. Finite sums commute with coordinate limits, hence $\operatorname{tr}D=\lim_k\operatorname{tr}D_k=r$. Therefore $D\in\mathcal D_r$. [step 1.2, F1, algebra]

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $(K,d)$ be a nonempty complete metric space and let $\Phi:K\to K$ be a
contraction with constant $0\le q<1$. In the SCF application, $K$ is a
complete invariant subset of the response-map domain from
[[def-self-consistent-projector-response-map]], with $d(X,Y)=\|X-Y\|_F$.
Then $\Phi$ has a unique fixed point $X_*$ and exact iterates
$X_{k+1}=\Phi(X_k)$ satisfy
$$d(X_k,X_*)\le q^k d(X_0,X_*).$$
For every $X\in K$,
$$d(X,X_*)\le\frac{d(X,\Phi(X))}{1-q}.$$
If computed updates $X_{k+1}\in K$ obey
$d(X_{k+1},\Phi(X_k))\le\eta_k$, then
$$e_{k+1}\le q e_k+\eta_k,\qquad e_k\le q^k e_0+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q^{k-1-j}\eta_j,$$
where $e_k=d(X_k,X_*)$ and $X_0$ is the supplied initial point.
Use the convention $q^0=1$, including when $q=0$.

actualproofparagraphs.2.1: For exact iterates, [F3] gives $d(X_{k+1},X_*)=d(\Phi(X_k),\Phi(X_*))\le qd(X_k,X_*)$. Induction from $k=0$ yields $d(X_k,X_*)\le q^k d(X_0,X_*)$. [step 1.1, given, F3, induction]
actualproofparagraphs.2.2: For any $X\in K$, [F2] identifies the SCF metric residual with $d(X,\Phi(X))$. The triangle inequality and contraction property give $d(X,X_*)\le d(X,\Phi(X))+d(\Phi(X),\Phi(X_*))\le d(X,\Phi(X))+q d(X,X_*).$ Since $1-q>0$, rearrangement proves the residual error bound. [given, step 1.1, F2, F3, algebra]

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Let $K\subseteq\mathcal D_r$ be nonempty, closed, and convex in Frobenius norm.
Suppose $F$ is $C^1$ on an open neighborhood of $K$, every matrix $F(D)$ there
has a strict $r$th gap so the gapped projector map $\Phi$ is defined, and for a
fixed $\alpha\in[0,1]$ the relaxed map
$$T_\alpha(D)=(1-\alpha)D+\alpha\Phi(D)$$
satisfies $T_\alpha(K)\subseteq K$. If a certified induced-norm bound
$$\|DT_\alpha(D)\|_{F\to F}\le q\qquad(D\in K),\qquad 0\le q<1,$$
holds, where $\|A\|_{F\to F}:=\sup_{\|H\|_F=1}\|A[H]\|_F$, then
$T_\alpha$ is a contraction on $K$ and its iterates converge to a unique fixed
point. The derivative is
$$DT_\alpha(D)=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha D\Phi(D).$$
The derivative bound is a separate hypothesis; $\alpha>0$ alone does not imply
contraction.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: For $D,E\in K$, convexity puts the segment $Z(t)=E+t(D-E)$ in $K$ for $t\in[0,1]$. By [F1] and [L1], $\Phi$ is defined along this segment; [F2] gives its local $C^1$ regularity. For an increment $H$, $T_\alpha(D+H)-T_\alpha(D)=(1-\alpha)H+\alpha(\Phi(D+H)-\Phi(D))$, so Frechet differentiability of $\Phi$ gives $DT_\alpha(D)=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha D\Phi(D)$. The chain rule [F5] on the segment gives $\frac d{dt}T_\alpha(Z(t))=DT_\alpha(Z(t))[D-E]$. Its norm is at most $q\|D-E\|_F$ by the assumed induced-norm bound; continuity follows from [F2] and [F6]. [given, F1, L1, F2, F5, F6, algebra]
actualproofparagraphs.2.1: Apply [F3] on $[0,1]$ to this path. It yields $\|T_\alpha(D)-T_\alpha(E)\|_F\le q\|D-E\|_F$, so $T_\alpha$ is a contraction on $K$. [step 1.1, F3]

source_evidence.fullclaim:
Assume the hypotheses and certificates in
[[alg-certified-scf-with-diis-safeguard]]: $\Phi$ is a $q$-contraction on the
complete invariant set $K$, its fixed point is $P_*$, the starting error is at
most $E_0$, and every baseline response error is at most $\eta_k$. Let $E_k$
be updated by that algorithm. Then every produced iterate obeys
$$\|P_k-P_*\|_F\le E_k\le q^kE_0+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q^{k-1-j}\eta_j.$$
An accepted DIIS candidate has certified error at most $qE_k$; the commutator
least-squares residual alone is not used as an error bound. If the procedure is
continued indefinitely with successful certificates and $\eta_k\to0$, then
$P_k\to P_*$; a finite update cap still may return budget exhaustion.
Use the convention $q^0=1$, including when $q=0$.

actualproofparagraphs.1.1: Initially $\|P_0-P_*\|_F\le E_0$ by input. Suppose $\|P_k-P_*\|_F\le E_k$. If the algorithm accepts candidate $Y=P_{k+1}$, [F2] gives a certified upper bound $\bar\rho(Y)$ for $\|Y-\Phi(Y)\|_F$ with $\bar\rho(Y)/(1-q)\le qE_k$. Applying [F1] at $Y$ proves $\|P_{k+1}-P_*\|_F\le qE_k=E_{k+1}$. [given, F1, F2]
actualproofparagraphs.2.1: If the baseline is used, its evaluator certifies $\|P_{k+1}-\Phi(P_k)\|_F\le\eta_k$. The triangle inequality and contraction give $\|P_{k+1}-P_*\|_F\le\eta_k+\|\Phi(P_k)-\Phi(P_*)\|_F\le\eta_k+q\|P_k-P_*\|_F\le qE_k+\eta_k=E_{k+1}.$ Thus induction proves $\|P_k-P_*\|_F\le E_k$ at every step. [given, step 1.1, F2, algebra]
actualproofparagraphs.3.1: By [F2], both update branches obey $E_{k+1}\le qE_k+\eta_k$ (accepted DIIS uses $\eta_k=0$ for this upper estimate). Iterating this scalar recurrence by induction gives $E_k\le q^kE_0+\sum_{j<k}q^{k-1-j}\eta_j$. [step 2.1, F2, induction, algebra]

source_evidence.case_anchor: At k=1, the convolution bound in proof step 3.1 has just eta_0 and readsE_1<=qE_0+eta_0, matching the baseline branch in proof step 2.1 and the sharper accepted-candidate bound in proof step 1.1.
